en.name: Orhan Mosque
description:
Orhan, who ascended the throne in 1324, captured Bursa in 1326 and entered the city with a magnificent ceremony. In order to develop the city, which had not yet expanded beyond its city walls, Orhan had the “Lower Fortress” built towards the east as well as the mosque complex that bears his name. Of the buildings that made up the complex, the *madrasa*, *mektep*, and *imaret* have not survived to the present day.  
In 1413, while Sultan Mehmed I was away in Rumelia on a military expedition, Karamanid Bey Mehmed II besieged Bursa. Hacı İvaz Pasha withdrew to the citadel and tried to defend the old city. In the last days of the one-month-long siege Karamanid Bey Mehmed Bey II set fire to both Great Mosque and Orhan Mosque. The fire damaged the portico and the main facade. According to the inscription above the entrance Orhan had this mosque built in 1339-1340, and after the Karamanid Bey Mehmed II destroyed it during his occupation of Bursa, the *Vizier* Bayezid Pasha repaired it on the order of Sultan Mehmed I in 1417.  
The five-bayed portico to the north of Orhan Mosque is very attractive with spandrels decorated in stone and brick. Orhan Mosque was planned to accommodate the needs of the wandering *Ahi dervishe*s by providing them with a lodging and meeting area. The domed *iwan*s that flank the domed central court were constructed with this aim in mind. A dome covers the main prayer hall and the *mihrab* is one of the most beautiful, coulourfully painted examples of an Anatolian stucco *mihrab*.

es.name: Mezquita de Orhan
description:
Orhan Bey, que había subido al trono en 1324, entró en Bursa, tras su toma en 1326, en medio de una espectacular ceremonia. Con el fin de desarrollar la ciudad, que no había sobrepasado aún los límites de la muralla, hizo construir al este la Fortaleza Baja y el complejo que lleva su nombre, del que no han sobrevivido ni la *madrasa*, ni el *mektep* ni el *imaret*.  
En 1413, mientras el sultán Mehmet I estaba lejos, en una expedición militar por Rumelia, el *bey* karamaní Mehmet II sitió Bursa. Hacı İvaz Paşa se retiró a la ciudadela y trató de defender la ciudad vieja. En los últimos días del asedio de un mes, el *bey* Mehmet II incendió la mezquita Mayor y la de Orhan. En el fuego resultaron dañados el pórtico y la fachada principal. En la inscripción de la puerta se lee que Orhan Bey hizo construir la mezquita en 1339-1349 y que, después de que el *bey* karamaní Mehmet II la destruyera durante la ocupación de Bursa, el visir Bayezid Paşa la hizo reparar en 1417 por orden del sultán Mehmet I.  
El pórtico del lado norte, de cinco crujías, atrae por la decoración de piedra y ladrillo de sus arcos. La mezquita se proyectó con la idea de atender las necesidades de reunión y alojamiento de los *derviches* itinerantes *ahi*, y a tal fin se construyeron los dos *iwan*s que flanquean el patio central. Una cúpula cubre la sala principal de oración; el *mihrab*, aunque pintado de colores, es uno de los más bellos *mihrab*s de estuco de Anatolia.

en.name: Erzini Mosque
description:
Built in the oldest part of town, this mosque is the last remaining piece of evidence of its time. It was constructed, it seems, in 999/1591, by one of the Andalusian families who had settled in Ttouan towards the end of the 9th/15th century. The minaret seems to have kept its original decoration. Only a geometric design, made of lime mortar, onto which *zellij* motifs are engraved, stands out in relief. The architectural feature which is true to this period is essentially the simplicity and miniature size of brick minarets.  
The interior of the mosque does not differ from conventional mosque interiors.

es.name: Mezquita Erzini
description: Situada en la zona más antigua de la ciudad, esta mezquita es el último testimonio de su época. Al parecer, fue construida en 999/1591 por una de las familias andalusíes instaladas en Tetuán a finales del siglo IX/XV. El alminar aparentemente conserva la decoración original. Solo hay en relieve un trazado geométrico en mortero de cal en el que están inscritos varios motivos en azulejo. El sello arquitectónico propio de esta época era, esencialmente, la simplicidad y pequeñez de los alminares de ladrillo. El interior de la mezquita no difiere de otros interiores tradicionales.

fr.name: Mosquée Erzini
description: Construite dans la partie la plus ancienne de la ville, cette mosquée est le dernier témoin de son époque. Elle fut construite, semble-t-il, en 999/ 1591, par une des familles andalouses installées à Tétouan à la fin du IXe/XVe siècle. Le minaret semble avoir gardé sa décoration d’origine. Seul un tracé géométrique en mortier de chaux, où des motifs en *zellige* viennent s’inscrire, est mis en relief. La marque architecturale propre à cette époque était essentiellement la simplicité et la petitesse des minarets de brique. L’intérieur de la mosquée ne diffère pas des intérieurs traditionnels.

en.name: Place Nejjarin
names: Place Nejjarin: Funduq, Fountain and Suq
description:
Situated strategically in the heart of the *medina*, in *Place Nejjarin*, the place of the Carpenters, named after the *suq* adjoining it, it links Bab Bujlud to the commercial and cultural core of the *medina* (Mulay Idriss, Qarawiyin). The *funduq*, the *suq* and the fountain, an architectural and urban scheme known as the “Nejjarine Complex”, rises up around the square.  
Built at the beginning of the 12th/18th century, the *funduq* was built for the storage of precious merchandise belonging to the men of the *makhzen* and to wealthy merchants. It seems that this monument held this role until the advent of the French Protectorate, when it had its function altered, becoming a police station in charge of the surveillance and repression of nationalists.  
This *funduq* is distinct for its portal which displays compositional unity: a horseshoe arch supported by two pillars of plain brick, paralleled by another polyfoiled arch made of sculpted plaster; bands run across above the arch, displaying either an inscription or a succession of carved plaster or wood arches. The interior, analogous to all other *funduq* interiors, was restored in 1998 and was converted into a Museum of Woodwork.  
The fountain next to the *funduq* is a principal component of this architectural development. It was built a century after the *funduq*, and in terms of its structure and decoration, it is reminiscent of the *funduq*’s portal. The basin, rectangular in cross-section, is covered in panels of *zellij* patterned geometrically. Its mid-section is dominated by a horseshoe blind arch, decorated with tiled mosaic rosette motifs. This bay is highlighted by a panelled arch which is framed in a rectangle of chiselled plaster panels. Lateral pillars, surfaced with *zellij* and sculpted plaster, support a wooden lintel on which an inscription in kursif lettering is engraved. The lintel is surmounted by wooden consoles which support a sculpted and painted canopy, which hangs over slightly and is covered in green-glazed roof tiles.  
As regards the *suq*, it dates from the Merinid era. A centre of production for wood products, from timber to mobile objects, it stands within a rectangular area, and is traversed by an alley full of stalls and workshops, which are more boringly built in brick and have plain cedarwood doors. Woodwork, wood being a very prized material in Morocco, comes from an ancient tradition, as is made evident by the preacher’s pulpit from the Andalusian Mosque dating from the 3rd/9th century, exhibited in the Batha museum.  
The friezes, sculpted corbels, the raised lintel porticoes made of cedarwood based on mortice and tenon joint-building techniques – they all attest to the high level attained in the field of woodworking during the Merinid era.

es.name: Plaza Neyyarin: funduq, fuente y suq
description:
La estratégica plaza de los Carpinteros —que toma el nombre del zoco colindante, el *suq* Neyyarin—, en pleno corazón de la *medina*, comunica Bab Bushlud con el nudo comercial y cultural de la *medina* (Mulay Idris, Qarawiyin). En torno a la plaza se encuentran el *funduq*, el *suq* y la fuente, conjunto arquitectónico y urbano que lleva el nombre de “Complejo Neyyarin”.  
El *funduq*, construido a comienzos del siglo XII/XVIII, estaba destinado a almacenar las mercancías preciosas de los hombres del Majzen y de ricos comerciantes. Al parecer, desempeñó ese papel hasta la implantación del Protectorado francés, momento en el que cambia de función y se convierte en comisariado encargado de la vigilancia y represión de los nacionalistas.  
El edificio se distingue por su portal de composición armoniosa: un arco de herradura que apoya en dos pilares de ladrillos, doblado por otro arco polilobulado en yeso cincelado; por debajo discurren fajas que portan una inscripción, es decir, una sucesión de arcadas en yeso cincelado o madera. El conjunto está coronado por ménsulas que sostienen un tejadillo en madera tallada. El interior, análogo al de todos los *funduq*s, fue restaurado en 1998 y convertido en Museo de la Madera.  
La fuente adyacente al *funduq* es uno de los elementos principales de este conjunto arquitectónico. Es posterior en un siglo al *funduq*, a cuyo portal recuerda por su estructura y decoración. El estanque, de sección rectangular, está recubierto de *zelish* que forma dibujos geométricos. Su parte mediana está dominada por un arco ciego, de herradura, decorado con rosetones de mosaico. Este vano está subrayado por un arco decorado con lambrequines, circunscrito en un rectángulo (arrabá) decorado con paneles de yeso. Los pilares laterales, recubiertos de *zelish* y yeso cincelado, sostienen un dintel de madera en el que hay una inscripción con caracteres cursivos. El dintel está coronado por ménsulas de madera que soportan un tejadillo de poco vuelo, tallado y pintado, recubierto de tejas verdes vidriadas.  
Por lo que se refiere al *suq*, data de la época meriní. Centro de producción de artículos y objetos de madera, desde carpintería hasta objetos mobiliarios, ocupa un espacio rectangular atravesado por un pasadizo al que se abren las tiendas y talleres, sobriamente construidos con ladrillo y cerrados por puertas de madera de cedro. El trabajo de la madera, material muy apreciado en Marruecos, deriva de una tradición muy antigua, como lo atestigua la silla de rezos de la mezquita de los Andalusíes expuesta en el Museo Batha, que data del siglo III/IX. Los frisos, canecillos esculpidos y pórticos con dinteles de cedro sobre soleras, con técnicas de ensamblaje por caja y espiga, atestiguan el alto nivel alcanzado en la época meriní por lo que se refiere al trabajo de la madera.

fr.name: Place Nejjarine: fondouk, fontaine et souk
description:
Située à une place stratégique au coeur de la médina, la place des Menuisiers, du nom du souk qui la jouxte, le souk Nejjarine, relie Bab Boujloud au noyau commercial et culturel de la médina (Moulay Idriss, Qaraouiyine). Autour de la place s’élèvent le fondouk, le souk et la fontaine, ensemble architectural et urbain portant le nom de “Complexe Nejjarine”.  
Construit au début du XIIe/XVIIIe siècle, le fondouk était destiné à entreposer les marchandises précieuses appartenant aux hommes du *makhzen* et aux riches négociants. Le monument a, semble-t-il, joué ce rôle jusqu’à l’avènement du Protectorat français où il changea de fonction et devint un commissariat chargé de surveiller et réprimer les nationalistes.  
Ce fondouk se distingue par son portail de composition harmonieuse: un arc outrepassé reposant sur deux piliers en briques pleines doublé d’un autre arc polylobé en plâtre sculpté; au-dessus de l’arc courent des bandeaux portant soit une inscription, soit une succession d’arcades en plâtre sculpté ou en bois. L’ensemble est couronné par des consoles qui servent à soutenir un grand auvent en bois sculpté. L’intérieur, analogue à tous les fondouks, a été restauré en 1998 et a été aménagé en musée du Bois.  
La fontaine adjacente au fondouk est une composante principale de cet ensemble architectural. Elle serait postérieure d’un siècle au fondouk dont elle rappelle, dans sa structure et sa décoration, le portail. Le bassin de section rectangulaire est recouvert de lambris de *zellige* à motifs géométriques. Sa partie médiane est dominée par une baie aveugle en plein cintre outrepassé, décorée de rosaces en mosaïque de faïence. Cette baie est soulignée par un arc en lambrequins encadré d’un rectangle décoré de panneau de plâtre ciselé. Les piliers latéraux, recouverts de *zellige* et de plâtre sculpté, soutiennent un linteau en bois où est gravée une inscription à caractères cursifs. Le linteau est surmonté de consoles en bois qui supportent un auvent sculpté et peint de faible saillie recouverte d’une toiture de tuiles vernissées vertes.  
Le souk quant à lui daterait de l’époque mérinide. Centre de production des articles et objets en bois, de la charpente aux objets mobiliers, il occupe un espace rectangulaire traversé par une allée sur laquelle s’ouvrent boutiques et ateliers, sobrement construits en brique, et fermés par des portes en bois de cèdre. Le travail du bois, matériau très prisé au Maroc, relève d’une tradition très ancienne comme en témoigne la chaire à prêcher de la mosquée des Andalous datant du IIIe/IXe siècle, exposée au musée Batha. Les frises, les corbeaux sculptés, les portiques à linteaux de cèdre sur semelle avec les techniques d’assemblage à tenons et à mortaise attestent le niveau élevé atteint par le travail du bois à l’époque mérinide.

ar.name: إبريق بتصميم خمسة حيوانات بشرية وشخص واقف
description: الإبريق هو ثنائي المخروط ذو مقبض وجسم مشكل بلون أصفر برتقالي ومموه بشكل مدولب ذو تزيين مطلي وتشكيلات مطلية بالذهب فوق زجاج أبيض. والإطار الطوقي المستقيم يستند إلى جسم ثنائي المخروط كبير مقطوع وعلى أرجل صغيرة متماوجة غير مزججة وشريط المقبض الشاقولي ذو مسند بشكل قرص مسطح مضاف له .وهناك شريط /عصابة ملتوية بلون أزرق –رمادي على الحافة. والإطار له إفريز عبارة عن مستطيلات رمادية – زرقاء مؤطرة من الأعلى والأسفل بلون أسود ومقسمة بخطوط حمراء شاقولية وكل لوحة مملوءة بنماذج أرابيسك دقيقة وشكل مركزي لورقة ذهبية مربعة صغيرة. والخط الأحمر والأسود يحدد الحدود بين العنق و الكتف. ويحتوي الكتف خمسة حيونات برؤوس بشرية ذات قبعات وأطواق وكل منها بلون مختلف (أزرق ، أحمر ، أخضر ، أزرق ، أحمر) تسير لجهة يسار المشاهد تجاه شجرة كرمة أو ينبوع  متناوبة ببراعم حمراء وزرقاء. والشخص مرتدي ثوبا ذو طراز طويل بلون أزرق وبني وقلنسوة مخروطية يقف خلف المشهد. وتشكيلات الأوراق الذهبية واقعة على كتفي الشخص وهناك ثلاثة أماكن على الجسم لكل حيوان برأس بشري وعناصر دائرية بينها. ويوجد سلسلة من البراعم بطراز خاص بالأسود والأحمر واقعة أسفل قمة العصابة ومجموعة ثانية تستند على الخط التزييني الأساسي. وهذه العصابة التزيينية هي بلون أخضر فاتح ومملوءة بنموذج وريدات رباعية البتلات مرسومة بالأسود مع مراكز بيضاء ونقاط زرقاء في الأعلى والأسفل مفصولة بمعينات زرقاء شاقولية و بعض المراكز ما تزال تحتقظ بعناصر الورق الذهبي المربع والنصف السفلي من الجسم غير مزين ما عدا سلسلة من العناصرالمزهرة البسيطة المرسومة بالأسود تماما تحت العصابة ويوجد تصميم مشابه مضاف أسفل الإطار الداخلي. والمقبض له نقش أسود كوفي ذو تشكيلات زرقاء على الجانبين ومسند أحمراللون . والزجاج متشقق بشكل كبير كليا و يوجد ست مناطق رئيسية مفقودة المعالم ومملوءة ومطلية.

en.name: Jug with Design of Five Sphinxes and a Standing Figure
description:
A biconical jug with handle and buff-colored composite body, wheel thrown with painted decoration and gilded highlights over white glaze. A straight collar rim sits on the large truncated biconical body on a small flared unglazed foot, a vertical strap handle with an applied flat disc thumb rest. There is a dark blue-gray scalloped band on the lip. The rim has a frieze of gray-blue rectangles outlined above and below in black and divided by vertical red lines; each panel is filled with delicate black arabesque patterns and a small square gold leaf central highlight.  
A red and black line defines the carination between neck and shoulder. The shoulder contains five spotted sphinxes with hats and collars, each a different color (blue, red, green, blue, red) walking to the viewer's left toward a vine or sprig with alternating red and blue buds. A figure in a long patterned blue robe and brown conical cap stands at the back of the procession. Gold leaf highlights the figure's shoulders, three areas on the body of each sphinx and the circular elements between them. A series of stylized buds in black and red sit below the top of the register and a second set rests on the decorative baseline. This decorative band is light green and filled with a pattern of red four-petaled rosettes drawn in black with white centers and blue dots above and below, separated by vertical blue lozenges. Some centers still preserve square gold foil elements.  
The bottom half of the body is undecorated except for a series of simple floral elements painted in black just under the band; a similar design is applied below the rim interior. The handle has a black *Kufic* inscription with blue highlights on the sides, the thumb rest is red. The glaze is badly cracked overall; six major areas of loss are in-filled and painted.
keywords: Jug; Ceramics; Glazed; Fritware; Underglaze; Painting; Overglaze; Enamel; Rayy; Iran; Asia; Persian

ar.name: صحن رسم عليه فارس.
description:
تمثل زخرفة الصحن فارساً، وتغطي المساحة كلها. تدل تقاطيع الوجه على أنه من أصل مغولي، وتمثل الزخرفة وريقات وأزهاراً ونباتاتٍ نافرةً. وتتميز هذه الزخرفة بإتقانها واختيار ألوانها و تثبيتها بأنها تتم بمراحل كثيرة تحضيراً وشياًً.  
ينتمي هذا النموذج إلى طبقة فنية تدعى بالفارسية هافت-رانغ وتعريبها (منعي أي سبعة ألوان):  
( أحمر، أزرق داكن، أخضر، أصفر، ذهبي، أبيض، أسود) مفروشة فوق طبقة زجاجية. ويبدو فيها أحياناً رسوم بارزة مغطاة بطبقة ذهبية كما في هذا النموذج.
تنتمي هذه القطعة إلى فئة الخزفيات التي تسمى الميناي، نظرا لاستعمال سبعة ألوان في الزخرف. وفي الفترة القديمة، كان قاشان  في الشمال الأوسط لإيران المركز الرئيسي لإنتاج خزفيات الميناي.

en.name: Bowl with horseman.
description:
The main decoration of the bowl consists of a large figure of a horseman, whose face clearly shows some Mongol features, on a background filled with plant shoots in relief.  
The decoration is characterised by a particularly delicate and elegant design painted in polychrome, with each colour requiring a separate firing.  
This piece belongs to a type known as *mina’i*’, in Persian ‘*haftrang*’(‘seven colours’). This technique effectively uses seven colours (red, blue, green, yellow, gold, white and black) applied on top of the glaze and occasionally, as in this case, with some details worked in relief and gilded.

This piece belongs to a type of ceramic known as *mina’i*, recognisable through the use of seven colours in its decoration. In antiquity, the main centre of production for *mina’i* ceramics was Kashan in central northern Iran.
holder: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art “Giuseppe Tucci”
keywords: Ceramics; minai; figurative decoration
partner: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art

es.name: Cuenco con jinete.
description:
Cuenco decorado, sobre un fondo de elementos vegetales en relieve, con una gran figura de jinete que ocupa todo el campo y cuyo rostro presenta evidentes rasgos mongoles.  
La ornamentación se caracteriza por un dibujo policromo muy esmerado y elegante, en el que cada color exige una cocción distinta.  
La pieza pertenece al tipo denominado *mina’i*, en persa *haft-rang* (“siete colores”). Esta técnica consiste en aplicar siete colores (rojo, azul, verde, amarillo, oro, blanco y negro) sobre el vidriado. A veces, como en este caso, algunos detalles se ejecutan en relieve y se doran.

Este ejemplar pertenece a un tipo de cerámica denominada *mina’i* (en persa *haft-rang*, “siete colores”) por el uso de siete colores en la decoración. El principal centro de producción de esta clase de cerámica en fue Kashan, en la región centroseptentrional de Irán.
holder: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”
dates: Siglo VI o VII de la Hégira / XII o XIII d. C.
keywords: cerámica; minai
partner: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental

fr.name: Coupe au cavalier.
description:
Le décor de cette coupe consiste en une grande figure de cavalier en pied, dont le visage présente des traits mongoliens évidents, sur fond d'entrelacs végétaux en relief.  
Ce décor se caractérise par un dessin particulièrement délicat et élégant peint en polychromie, où chaque couleur exige une cuisson à part.  
Cette pièce appartient à la classe appelée “minaï”, en persan “haft-rang” (“sept couleurs”) ; cette technique utilise effectivement sept couleurs (rouge, bleu, vert, jaune, or, blanc, noir) étendues sur la glaçure et parfois, comme ici, certains détails sont exécutés en relief et dorés.

Cette pièce appartient à la classe de céramiques appelées *mina'i*, à cause de l'utilisation de sept couleurs dans le décor. Le principal centre de production de céramiques *mina'i* fut, dans l'Antiquité, Kashan, dans le centre-nord de l'Iran.
holder: Musée des civilisations | Musée d'art oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”
dates: VIe-VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIe-XIIIe siècle J.-C.).

it.name: Coppa con cavaliere.
description: La decorazione della coppa consiste in una grande figura di cavaliere a tutto campo, il cui volto presenta evidenti tratti mongoli, sopra un fondo campito da tralci vegetali a rilievo. La decorazione è caratterizzata da un disegno particolarmente delicato ed elegante dipinto in policromia, ove ogni colore richiede una cottura separata. L'esemplare appartiene alla classe denominata minâ' i, in persiano haft-rang, (“sette colori”): questa tecnica usa effettivamente sette colori (rosso, blu, verde, giallo, oro, bianco, nero) stesi sopra l'invetriatura e, a volte, come in questo caso, alcuni particolari sono eseguiti in rilievo e coperti da dorature.

Questo esemplare appartiene alla classe di ceramiche denominate *minâ' i*, per via dell'uso di sette colori nella decorazione. Il principale centro di produzione delle ceramiche *minâ' i* fu, nell'antichità, Kashan, nell'Iran Centro-settentrionale.

keywords: ceramica; minâ'i; decorazione figurativa
partner: Museo delle Civiltà | Museo d’arte orientale “Giuseppe Tucci”

en.name: Abdul Baha Abbas (1844–1921)
short_description: Born in Tehran, Abbas left Iran because of religious persecution. He travelled widely in Egypt, Europe and the United States. In 1913 he settled in Haifa where he founded the religious sect of Baha'i.

en.name: Old City Walls and Citadel
description:
Tartus was the town held the longest by the Crusaders in the Levant. The buildings erected during their long stay, especially the superbly preserved cathedral, give a good impression of the general shape of a medieval coastal city in the Near East during the 6th/12th century.  
Tartus sprang up as a satellite settlement off Arwad Island, which was the centre of the settlement pattern in ancient times. Tartus rose to prominence in the Romano-Byzantine period, its fame enhanced by two early Christian relics: the altar, according to legend, consecrated by the Apostle Peter during his short stay; the miraculous icon, allegedly one of four painted by Saint Luke. Disregarding a short period of Byzantine reconquest in the second half of the 4th/10th century, Tartus was in Muslim hands from the Arab conquests in the first half of the 1st/7th century up until the advent of the Crusades. While the army of the First Crusade briefly occupied the town in 492/1099, the firm establishment of Crusader control was not realised until 495/1102, when one of the Crusader leaders, Raymond of Saint Gilles, made it his base for the conquest of the future County of Tripoli. The campaign of Nur al-Din in 546/1152 succeeded in occupying and devastating the town, which led the bishop to transfer the lordship of the settlement to the Order of the Temple in return for protection. The town of Tartus then became the northern headquarters of the Templars. Even though Salah al-Din’s army destroyed the town and part of the citadel in 594/1188, the Templars resisted them in the donjon. Tartus, rebuilt after Saladin’s departure, remained in Crusader hands until in 590/1291.  
A surrounding ditch and town wall with rectangular projecting towers defended the medieval town of Tartus. The part of the gateway most intact is in the western part of town, and it is the best-preserved Crusader town gate in the region. The gate stood at the point where the town wall joined the fortifications of the citadel. The Templars built the citadel in the north-western corner of the walled rectangle, with direct access to the town, the sea and the fields to the north.  
The castle plan is oval-shaped and concentric, with a double circuit of walls on its landward side, surrounded by rock-cut moats. The enclosures were built of large bossed ashlars, a favourite construction material of the Templars, and flanked by large oblong towers, which is also characteristic of 7th-/13th-century Templar defensive architecture. At one point, the inner wall survived to its full height (25.5 m), with good examples of different kinds of loopholes on several of the preserved levels. The high inner wall was supported in the interior by huge vaulted ranges, which were also used as storage areas.  
The main entrance to the citadel was through an enormous gatehouse, which now functions as a mosque. Though much overbuilt later by houses, the interior of the castle still preserves the most important elements characteristic of the fortifications of the military orders. One was the large rectangular building on two levels, the upper storey most probably containing the Great Hall of the knights. Another was the chapel, a typically austere building covered with gothic ribbed-vaults. The third, main element of the castle was the donjon, which stood by the seaside. Its shooting galleries (which opened from a glacis at ground level) were constructed around an older donjon, possibly that which held out against Salah al-Din. Separated from the rest of the castle by a large ditch, the donjon, with its long seaward faade, had two flanking towers to provide additional defences.  
Leaving the bases on the south-west corner tower of the inner castle, one reaches the sloping glacis of the southwest tower of the town wall, opposite the entrance to the harbour, from which Arwad Island is reached. Being the only habitable island on the Syrian coast and offering the best natural harbour of the region, Arwad was an important military base for the Templars, where they held out until 701/1302. Their castle was in the middle of the island, but was largely demolished and remodelled in later periods.

de.name: Altar und Orgelchor
description: Der 1730 im Gewölbebereich erneuerte Chorraum wurde anläßlich des 1748er Friedensfestes noch mit einer neuen Orgelempore ausgestattet, deren leicht kurvierte Balustrade durch ihre schlichte Eleganz besticht. Aufgrund der farblichen Fassung der Stuckdekorationen – oben spätes Régence, unten frühes Rokoko – erhält der Altarraum eine eigenständige, fast bildhafte Qualität. Das Deckenfresko verbildlicht die drei Theologische Tugenden: Glaube, Liebe, Hoffnung. Wie bei der Kanzel befinden sich auch neben dem Altar Gemälde mit Szenen des Christuslebens: Taufe, Auferstehung, Pfingsten, Abendmahl. Die beiden wichtigsten kultischen Komponenten – Altar und Kanzel – sind so inhaltlich verklammert und ganz unter die Heilslehre Christi gestellt.
dates:

1673/74 Gemälde  
1730 Orgel und Gewölbedekoration

en.name: Altar and choir
description: The choir, oriented to the west, was renewed in 1730 in the contemporary Rococo style. On the occasion of the centennial of the Peace of 1648 a new gallery for the organ was installed. The slightly curved stucco is captivating in its simple elegance, its colour highlighting the choir. Although the gallery continues in the choir, the coloured Regency and Rococo stucco establishes a discrete, almost scenographic quality. The fresco on the ceiling shows the three theological virtues: Faith, Hope and Charity. Around the altar, as at the pulpit, paintings depict scenes from the Life of Christ: the Baptism, Resurrection, Pentecost and Last Supper. The two most important ritualistic elements in the church – altar and pulpit – together harmonise in form and content, dedicated fully to the teachings of Christ.
dates: c. 1653: retable; 1673/74: paintings; 1730: organ and decoration of the vault; 1748: renovation of the gallery and organ; 1767: altar
artist: Johann Heiss (1640–1704), Johann Ulrich Mayr (1630–1704), Johannes Spillenberger (1628–1679), Josef Werner (1637–1710); Johann Georg Bergmüller (1688–1762); Johann Esaias Nilson (active 1721–1728); Ignaz Wilhelm Verhelst (1729–1792)
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: National Palace of Mafra
description:
Symmetrically organised, the building evolves from a central axis: the basilica flanked by the palace façades, the king's apartments at the north end, and the queen's on the south. At the back there is a convent, originally intended for the Order of St. Francis, which has at its nucleus a uniquely well-preserved 18th-century hospital.  
Altogether the palace occupies 38,000 m2 and has 1,200 rooms and 4,700 doors and windows. The high points of the Basilica are the ensemble of statues made by Italian masters, part of The Royal Commission that also comprises an important collection of 18th-century Italian and Portuguese paintings, two Flemish-made carillons with 92 bells, retables from the Mafra school of sculpture, and a set of six organs.

The National Palace of Mafra is Portugal’s most important Baroque building, comprising a royal palace, a basilica and a Franciscan convent within which is a well-preserved 18th-century hospital. The palace houses the remarkable Royal Commission, a collection of Italian sculptures and Portuguese and Italian paintings, two carillons and six historical organs as well as precious gold artefacts and church ornaments.
type: Secular and religious architecture: Palace, Convent with Hospital and Basilica
artist: Architect: Johan Friedrich Ludwig (João Frederico Ludovice, active 1718–1746); interior designers/architect (of library): Manuel Caetano de Sousa (1738–1802); sculptors: Carlo Monaldi (1683–1760), Giovanni Battista Maini (1690–1752), Fillippo della Valle (1698–1768), Alessandro Giusti (1715–1799); organ makers: Peres Fontanes, Machado Cerveira (both active between 1792–1807); carillons: Nicholas Levache, Willem Witlockx (both active 1730); painters: Francisco Vieira de Matos (known as Vieira Lusitano 1699–1783), Agostino Masucci (1690–1768), Francesco Trevisani (1656–1746); mural painters: Cyrilo Volkmar Machado (1748–1823), Domingos Sequeira (1768–1837), Bernardo de Oliveira Góis (active 18th century)
history:
Taking advantage of the prosperity granted by the Brazilian gold afflux, King D. João V ordered construction of the Palace in the hope that this initiative would bless him with the birth of a male heir to the throne. The first stone was set in 1717, under the direction of the architect Johan Frederich Ludwig.  
The so-called “Real Obra” was the first Portuguese school of Fine Arts, particularly for architects, stonemasons, carpenters, cabinetmakers and painters; in 1753, King D. João V’s son, King D. José I, implemented a School of Sculpture there under the direction of the Italian Alessandro Giusti.  
Mafra was King D. João V’s favourite palace, and at the end of the 18th century, he commissioned the mural paintings and a new ensemble of six organs for the Basilica. Although the palace was never a permanent royal residence, it was frequently visited by royalty for hunting in the extensive park or to attend religious festivities.  
In the aftermath of the monarchy’s last days, it was from Mafra that the last Portuguese sovereign, D. Manuel II, left to go into exile in 1910.

pt.name: *Palácio Nacional de Mafra*
description:
Construído em pedra lioz da região, o edifício organiza-se simetricamente em dois corpos justapostos. O primeiro, a poente, tem ao centro a Basílica, ladeada pelo Palácio do Rei, a norte, e pelo Palácio da Rainha, a sul. O segundo, a nascente, inclui o Convento, originalmente destinado à Ordem de S. Francisco da Província da Arrábida.  
Ocupa uma área de cerca de 38.000 m2, com 1.200 divisões e 4.700 portas e janelas. Na Basílica, destacam-se a colecção de escultura italiana de encomenda real, os retábulos da Escola de Escultura de Mafra e o conjunto de seis órgãos históricos, único no mundo. Possui ainda uma colecção de pintura italiana e portuguesa do século XVIII e dois carrilhões com noventa e dois sinos, encomendados na Flandres. O núcleo conventual inclui uma rara enfermaria do século XVIII, ainda *in situ*.

Conjunto arquitectónico barroco, formado por um Paço Real, uma Basílica e um Convento. Possui importantes colecções de escultura italiana, de pintura italiana e portuguesa, uma biblioteca única, bem como dois carrilhões, seis órgãos históricos e um hospital do século XVIII.
type: Arquitectura religiosa e secular. Palácio, convento, basílica, biblioteca.
artist: Arquitecto: Johan Friedrich Ludwig / João Frederico Ludovice (activo entre 1718–1746); desenho de interiores/arquitecto (Biblioteca): Manuel Caetano de Sousa (1738–1802); escultores: Carlo Monaldi (1683–1760), Giovanni Battista Maini (1690–1752), Fillipo della Valle (1698–1768), Alessandro Giusti (1715–1799); organeiros: Peres Fontanes e Machado Cerveira (ambos activos entre 1792 e 1807); pintores: Francisco Vieira de Matos (conhecido como Vieira Lusitano, 1699–1783), Agostino Masucci (1690–1768), Francesco Trevisani (1656–1746); pintura mural: Cyrilo Volkmar Machado (1748–1823), Domingos Sequeira (1768–1837), Bernardo de Oliveira Góis (activo no final do séc. XVIII); mestres carrilhaneiros: Nicholas Levache, Willem Witlockx (activos em 1730).
history:
Mandado erguer por D. João V no cumprimento de um voto de sucessão, é o maior edifício barroco português, com uma magnificência apenas possível devido ao ouro que então afluía do Brasil.  
A Real Obra, cuja primeira pedra foi lançada em 1717 sob a direcção de João Frederico Ludovice, foi a primeira escola de Belas Artes do país, valorizada por D. José I, em 1753, com uma escola de escultura dirigida pelo italiano Alessandro Giusti.  
Foi o paço preferido de D. João VI, que encomendou, no final do século XVIII, pinturas murais e um novo conjunto de seis órgãos para a Basílica.  
Não sendo residência permanente da família real, o palácio foi sempre visitado pelos reis para assistirem a festas religiosas ou para caçarem na Tapada e foi daqui que D. Manuel II, último rei de Portugal, partiu para o exílio, em 1910.

en.name: Oriental Festival at the Turin Exhibition, 1911
names: *Le Esposizioni del 1911. Torino. La vita orientale e la grande kermesse*
short_description: In 1911 the city of Turin organized an International Exhibition in the Valentino park, on the banks of the Po River. Beyond the Isabella Bridge another huge park was built to house entertainment and attractions. One of the most popular attractions was the so-called "Kermesse Orientale", in which the public experienced the illusion of making a journey through the different parts of the Eastern world. Five new areas were built, according to photographs taken at the time. The first one represented Arabian, Egyptian, Tunisian and Turkish environments while the fourth area reproduced Japan and India. The park also showcased a harem, a mosque and a Moorish school and the visitors could enjoy belly dancing shows and walks on camelback.

de.name: Altes Tiroler Landhaus
description: Der um einen rechteckigen Binnenhof angelegte Bau besteht aus einem breit gelagerten Haupttrakt mit Straßenfassade, Vestibül, Treppenhaus und Sitzungssaal im zweiten Obergeschoss. Daran schließen im rechten Winkel zwei wesentlich schmalere und etwas niedrigere Flügel an, die den Hof nach Norden und Süden einfassen. Gegen die vierte Seite abgeschlossen wird dieser durch die von Gumpp 1725-28 errichtete Landhauskapelle St. Georg, die über Zugänge mit den Hofflügeln verbunden ist. Neben dem großen Landtagssaal, dessen Fresken von Cosmas Damian Asam stammen, ist auch der Kongress-Saal im nördlichen Flügel mit seiner späteren Rokokostukkatur ein prächtiger, dem Zweck politischer Repräsentation dienender Festsaal.

Das Haus der Tiroler Landstände ist der monumentalste Barockpalast Innsbrucks und zugleich der größte und bedeutendste Profanbau des Hofbaumeisters Georg Anton Gumpp. Als herausragendes Symbol der selbstbewussten Standesvertretung sind Architektur und Ausstattung von besonderer Pracht und künstlerischer Qualität geprägt. Die mächtige Dreiflügelanlage mit angeschlossener Kapelle bildet neben der Hofburg das repräsentative politische Zentrum der Landeshauptstadt.
artist:
Architekt: Georg Anton Gumpp (1682-1754)  
Fresken: Cosmas Damian Asam (1686-1739)  
Bildhauerarbeiten: Ingenuin Lechleitner (1676-1731); Nikolaus Moll (1676-1754)  
Stuck: Anton Gigl (1700-1769); Franz Singer u. a.
history: Seit 1613 tagten die Landstände im “Haus zum goldenen Engel”, dessen Versammlungssaal aber für den vollen Landtag zu klein war. 1666 erfolgte der Umzug in die „Hofplattnerei“, die sich jedoch in schlechtem baulichen Zustand befand. Im Zuge des Bedeutungsgewinns der Tiroler Stände im frühen 18. Jahrhundert erfolgte schließlich ein Neubau, errichtet 1725-28 durch Georg Anton Gumpp unter dem Patronat des Brixener Fürstbischofs und des Landeshauptmanns von Tirol. Die erste Ausstattungsphase dauerte bis 1734, der Kongresssaal wurde um 1758 stuckiert. In der Zeit Maria Theresias nahm die Bedeutung der Ständevertretung stark ab. Heute ist das Landhaus der Sitz des Tiroler Landtags.
keywords: Profanbau; Palais; Festsaal; Landtag; Stände

en.name: Old Federal State Parliament
description: The building, arranged around a rectangular inner courtyard, consists of a wide main wing with a street façade, vestibule, staircase and assembly hall on the second floor. Two narrower and lower wings adjoin it at right angles and enclose the courtyard to the north and south. The fourth side is composed of the parliament chapel of St George, built by Gumpp between 1725 and 1728 with entrances connecting it to the wings. In addition to the parliament hall with the Asam frescos, the congress hall in the north wing is a magnificent festive hall designed for the purpose of political representation.

The House of the Estates of Tyrol is the most monumental of Innsbruck’s Baroque palaces as well as the largest and most important secular building of the court master builder Georg Anton Gumpp. As a symbol of the self confident representation of the estates, the architecture and furnishings are of a special grandeur and artistic quality. Together with the Hofburg, the three-wing complex with connected chapel forms the representative centre of the state capital.
artist: Estates of the Province of Tyrol

Architect: Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); frescos: Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739); sculptural work: Ingenuin Lechleitner (1676–1731); Nikolaus Moll (1676–1754); stuccowork: Anton Gigl (1700–1769); Franz Singer (1688–1740), Johann Singer [n.d.], et al.
history: Since 1613 the estates convened in the “Haus zum goldenen Engel” (House of the Golden Angel), however its assembly room was too small for the full parliament. In 1666 it was moved to the “Hofplattnerei”, but the building was in poor condition. With the growing importance of the estates of Tyrol in the early 18th century a new building was constructed between 1725 and 1728 by Georg Anton Gumpp under the patronage of the prince-bishop of Brixen and the governor of Tyrol. The first period of interior design work ended in 1734, stucco was applied to the congress hall in 1758. Today the Landhaus is the seat of the Tyrolean parliament.
keywords: Secular building; palace; festive hall; state parliament; estates

en.name: Fort-l’Empereur
description:
This fort was part of the exterior defensive complex of al-Djazair (Algiers), located about 1,000 metres away from the medina. It was designed to protect the southern part of the rampart.  
  
It has had several names, including that of its builder, Moulay Hassan. He erected it on the site of the battery that emperor Charles V had installed to bombard the city during his attempt to seize it in 947 / 1541. A storm ruined his plans, but the emperor made the Ottomans aware of the strategic importance of the site. From this point forward the fort would be known as Fort of the Emperor, the name it still bears today.  
  
Because of its impressive size and hilltop location at an elevation of 230 metres, it was visible from a distance; thus it came to be known as *Bordj Ettaous*, or Fort of the Peacocks.  
  
It had a rectangular shape, 150 metres long by 100 metres wide. Its walls were 10 metres high. It is no longer open to the public, but one can estimate the height of its walls and observe its prominent position on a hill above Malika-Gaid Boulevard, which crosses the Tagarins District and leads to el-Biar.  
  
The fort was built in several stages. The first circular tower, erected by Hassan Pasha after the departure of the Spaniards, was completed in 951 / 1545. Don Philippe, the new sovereign of Spain, reassembled the fleet in Cadiz in 988 / 1580. Alerted by his war preparations, the inhabitants of Algiers felt threatened. Hassan Veneziano, then governor of al-Djazair, built bastions at the four cardinal points, surrounding the central space where the first tower was located, thereby creating a square enclosure. This was further secured by a ditch that separated the bastions in case of retreat. A rampart along the ditch was pierced by embrasures placed in order to slow the advance of attackers.  
  
The fort is inaccessible from the sea due to a very steep rocky slope. This detail did not escape Lieutenant Boutin, charged by the French government with establishing an inventory of the city’s fortifications at the beginning of the 19th century. He advocated an attack on the fort from the west towards the land.  
  
On 3 July 1830, at dawn, the French army concentrated its fire on that facade. For several hours the fort stood against a hail of bullets. As the battle neared an end, the remaining survivors withdrew, leaving one of their own to blow up the fort. The central tower disappeared. The rest was damaged. Stones fell on the city, causing panic among the inhabitants of the Casbah. After the fort fell, the city soon followed.

fr.name: Fort-l’Empereur
description:
Ce fort faisait partie de l’ensemble défensif extérieur de la médina, dont il est éloigné d’environ mille mètres. Il était destiné à protéger la partie sud du rempart.  
  
Il a porté plusieurs noms dont celui de Bordj Moulay Hassan, son bâtisseur. Celui-ci l’érigea à l’emplacement de la batterie que l’empereur Charles-Quint avait installée pour bombarder la ville lorsqu’il tenta de la prendre en 947/1541. Il en fut empêché par une tempête qui ruina ses projets mais il fit prendre conscience aux Ottomans de l’importance stratégique du lieu. De là découle la deuxième appellation du Fort, Fort-l’Empereur, qu’il porte encore aujourd’hui.  
  
Du fait de sa superficie et de sa position élevée sur une colline culminant à 230 mètres d’altitude, il était visible de loin : on lui donna donc le nom de Bordj Ettaous ou fort des Paons.  
  
Il avait la forme d’un grand rectangle de 150 m de long et de 100 m de large. Ses murs s’élevaient à 10 mètres. Aujourd’hui, occupé par l’Armée, il n’est plus accessible, mais on devine la hauteur de ses murs et sa situation proéminente sur une butte au-dessus du boulevard Malika-Gaid qui le longe en contrebas, traversant le quartier des Tagarins et menant à el-Biar.  
  
Le fort fut construit en plusieurs étapes. L’érection d’une première tour circulaire par Hassan Pacha, après le départ des Espagnols, est terminée en 951/1545. En 988/1580, le nouveau souverain d’Espagne, Don Philippe, réunit sa flotte à Cadix. Les habitants d’Alger, alertés par ses préparatifs de guerre, se sentent menacés. Hassan Veneziano, alors gouverneur d’al-Djazaïr, fait élever quatre bastions, aux quatre points cardinaux, entourant l’espace central où se trouvait la première tour, donnant à l’ensemble une forme carrée. Le tout fut renforcé par un fossé séparant les bastions deux à deux en cas de retraite. Un parapet longeant le fossé et percé d’embrasures était censé ralentir la progression des assaillants.  
  
Côté mer, il est inaccessible en raison d’une pente rocheuse très abrupte. Ce détail n’a pas échappé au lieutenant Boutin, chargé par le gouvernement français d’établir un état des lieux des fortifications de la ville au début du XIXe siècle. Il préconisa, en effet, une attaque du fort par le côté ouest donnant vers les terres.  
  
Le 3 juillet 1830 à l’aube, c’est sur cette façade que l’armée française concentra son feu. Le fort résista plusieurs heures au déluge des boulets. Lorsque l’issue du combat fut proche, les derniers survivants se retirèrent en laissant un des leurs pour faire exploser le fort. La tour centrale disparut. Le reste fut endommagé. Des pierres retombèrent jusque sur la ville, semant la panique parmi les habitants de la Casbah. Quand le fort tomba, la ville ne tarda pas à le suivre.

en.name: *Medbasa* (Dibs/date-molasses Extraction Room)
description: Many markets in the UAE had medbasas, which were special rooms that contained grooves in the floor for collecting *dibs* (date molasses). Date palm leaf bags full of dates were piled on top of each other above the grooved floor. The combined weight of the bags pressed molasses out of the dates. The molasses drained between the grooves and into a pot where it could be collected and sold. Several *medabasa* rooms still exist in Sharjah and can be visited at Al Hisn (Fort) Museum and Souq Shinasiyya.
dates: Hegira mid 14th century / AD mid 20th century
keywords: date molasses; date; dates; medbasa; dibs

en.name: Chapel of Santo André
description: This Chapel or hermitage, is one of a series built in this region, all of them characterised by cylindrical buttresses at the corners and along the sides. This one also has a porch or covered atrium, and consists of one single nave and a square chapel, crowned by decorative battlements. The interior is very simple with ribbed vaulting in the apse.

de.name: Fassade Westflügel und Portal
description:
Ende des 17. Jahrhunderts wurden der Westflügel und sein Turm mit geschwungener Haube errichtet. Da man den Klosterkomplex von dieser Seite betritt, erhielt der Flügel die Hauptfassade mit interessanter Pilaster-Ordnung: im mittleren Bereich und auf der rechten Seite des Gebäudes sind sie perfekt angeordnet. Zwei Paare rahmen die Mittelachse des Turms, drei Paare Doppelpilaster und drei einzelne Pilaster trennen die fünf Fenster rechts. Auf der linken Seite gibt es nur drei Fensterachsen, vielleicht waren es einmal vier, die Verteilung der Pilaster ist – wohl deswegen – unregelmäßig. Der Abstand zwischen den drei Doppelpilaster-Paaren variiert von Paar zu Paar. Die zwei einzelnen Pilaster links außen könnten ein Doppelpilaster-Paar mit großem Zwischenraum oder auch zwei einzelne Pilaster sein, die ein nicht mehr existierendes Fenster rahmten. Ob diese Pilaster-Ordnung die ursprüngliche Idee des/der Architekten war?  
Kaum jemand wird sich an der unregelmäßigen Anordnung der Pilaster stören, da das Marmorportal mit der krönenden Statue der Muttergottes und dem Jesuskind, der künstlerische Höhepunkt der Fassade, alle Aufmerksamkeit auf sich zieht. Zwei Heilige (Adalbero und Kilian) stehen zu ihren Seiten. Der Bildhauer hatte einen großen Sinn für Humor (der Abt muss ihn auch gehabt haben): denn trotz der heiligen Gesellschaft darüber treiben Engel und Putten oberhalb des Wappens von Abt Severin Blass ihre Späße. Ein besonders schlimmer spielt mit einer Bischofsmütze, zwei andere helfen ihm, sie aufzusetzen. Jedes Detail des Portals ist fein herausgearbeitet, das Stück ist als gesamtes ein barockes Meisterwerk.

en.name: Façade West wing and portal
description:
At the end of the 17th century the West wing and its tower with curved hood roof were built. As one enters the monastery complex at this side, the wing has the main façade with an interesting pilaster order: on the middle part with the tower and on the right side of the building they are perfectly arranged. Two pairs frame the tower´s middle axis, three pairs of double pilasters and three single pilasters separate the five windows on the right. On the left side there are only three window axes, maybe there were at some time four, the distribution of the pilasters is – probably because of that – irregular. The interval between the three double pilaster pairs varies from pair to pair. The two single pilasters on the far left could be a double pilaster pair with a big space between, but they could also be two single pilasters framing a no longer existent window. Who knows if this pilaster order was the original idea of the architect(s)?  
Hardly anyone will notice the pilasters´ irregular order as the façade´s artistic highlight, the marble portal with the crowning statue of the Holy Virgin and the Baby Christ, will captivate the viewer. Two saints (Adalbero and Kilian) are at their sides. The sculptor had a great sense of humour (the abbot must have had too): unimpressed by the holy society above, angels and putti are frolicking around abbot Severin Blass´s crest. A naughty one is playing with a mitre; two others help him to put it on. Every detail on the portal is finely carved out, the thing is as a whole a baroque masterwork.
dates: End of 17th century West wing; 1693 marble portal
artist: Unknown: West wing; Jakob Auer: marble portal

en.name: Lidded bowl (*sahan*)
description: A deep bowl on a rounded foot, with lid – *sahan* (Ar. *sân*) – was used for serving food. The bell-shaped lid is decorated with vegetal and geometric motives, with a small, circular, star-like handle on the top. The same type of leafy, vegetal pattern is engraved on the bowl.
keywords: lidded bowl; tableware; sahan; sân; copper; Ottoman Balkans
materials: Copper; tinned, hammering, engraving, black compound

en.name: Vase
description:
This is a design by Marie Kirschner, a painter, architect, decorator and designer of textiles, glass and ceramics, born in the present-day Czech Republic. This example was personally signed by Kirschner (with the monogram “MK”), which she apparently only did for pieces she sold herself.  
  
Educated in Paris and Berlin, Kirschner began specializing in home accessory design around 1880. In 1900, she began working as an interior decorator in Berlin. She focused primarily on glasswork between 1902 and 1914, producing around 270 examples of vases, containers and figures, all varied in form and organic in nature.  
  
Kirschner worked as a glass designer for the Johann Lötz Witwe factory in Klostermühle, Bohemia (modern-day Czech Republic). The factory had become the most renowned glass manufacturer around the turn of the twentieth century, thanks to its boldly coloured and iridescent designs, which were called *Phänomen* (phenomenon). Kirschner made her first contribution to the company between 1897 and 1898, and served as its director of design from 1900 to 1904.
keywords: Glasfabrik Lötz Witwe; Phänomen

es.name: Jarrón
description:
Es un diseño de Marie Kirschner, pintora, arquitecta, decoradora y diseñadora de tejidos, vidrio y cerámica procedente de la actual República Checa. Este ejemplar presenta firma personal de Kirschner (monograma formado por las iniciales MK) lo que, según parece, solo realizaba en las piezas que ella misma vendía.  
Kirschner se formó en París y Berlín, especializándose hacia 1880 en la creación de accesorios para la casa. En 1900 empezó a desarrollar su actividad en Berlín como decoradora de interiores. De 1902 a 1914 trabajó fundamentalmente el vidrio, realizando unos doscientos setenta modelos de jarrones, recipientes y figuras de formas diferentes, de carácter orgánico.  
Trabajó como diseñadora de vidrio para la fábrica Johann Lötz Witwe, situada en Klostermühle, en Bohemia (actual República Checa), que se había convertido en la manufactura de vidrio más célebre en torno a 1900 gracias a sus diseños de colores fuertes e iridiscentes, denominados “Phänomen” (fenómeno). Su primera contribución para dicha firma data de 1897-98, y de 1900 a 1904 fue directora de diseño de la misma.
keywords: Glasfabrik Lötz Witwe; Phänomen

en.name: Church of San Niccolò lo Regale
names: Church of San Nicolò lo Regale
description:
The church is to be found in the quarter of San Giovanni, facing west towards the right-bank of the port-canal, which forms the real fulcrum of the city. The terminal for centuries of sea routes from the time of the Phoenicians, and being navigable for some long distance, it was a most important point of reference also in the Arab era and later in that of the Normans both from the military and commercial point of view. The construction of the church dates back to the period of the County, around 1124 (Scuderi, 1978). It is based on a central plan of the Greek cross, inscribed in a square of about 10.5 m. per side, with the eastern side having three protruding apses, with a larger, more projected central apse. Unfortunately the original interior configuration has been destroyed on account of the notable transformations carried out over time, but there is certainly evidence that originally a cupola covered the crossway and that the arms of the cross were furnished with wooden roofing with inlays and gilding. The cupola stands over a wide and vast cubic tambour leaning on four columns, and has been reconstructed several times during restoration works.  
The surrounding walls bore decorations in marble and mosaic on their internal side, analogous to the paving. The external walls have maintained their original configurations, characterised by a continuous series of multiple blind arches *a rincasso*, enframing the three ogival windows, which open on each side. During the baroque period the outside of the church underwent considerable rearrangement, such as the opening of a portal in the centre of the main apse, closed up in the course of the 20th-century restoration tending to confer its original appearance to the building. The remains of a villa (or of a mansion) datable to between the 3rd and 4th centuries were discovered under the church with polychrome fresco walls and mosaic paving.

es.name: Iglesia de San Nicolás el Real
description: La iglesia se encuentra en el barrio de San Giovanni, que da por su parte occidental a la orilla derecha del puerto-canal, verdadero eje de la ciudad, muelle de seculares rutas marítimas desde la edad fenicia y, al ser navegable durante un largo tramo, importantísimo punto de referencia también en la época árabe y, posteriormente, en la normanda, tanto desde el punto de vista militar como comercial. La construcción de la iglesia parece remontarse al periodo del Condado, alrededor de 1124 (Scuderi, 1978). Presenta una planta central en cruz griega, inscrita en un cuadrado de 10,5 m de lado en cuyo flanco oriental surgen tres ábsides sobresalientes, el central más amplio y profundo. Lamentablemente, la configuración original del interior se destruyó con las considerables transformaciones obradas a lo largo del tiempo, pero se tienen noticias ciertas de que el crucero estaba cubierto en origen por una cúpula y los brazos de la cruz por techos de madera con taracea y dorados. La cúpula, que se alza sobre un gran tambor cúbico sostenido por cuatro columnas, se ha reconstruido varias veces en las restauraciones. Los muros tenían en su cara interna decoración en mármol y mosaico, análoga a la del pavimento. El paramento mural exterior ha conservado la configuración original, caracterizada por una serie continua de arcos ciegos múltiples rehundidos que enmarcaban las tres ventanas ojivales abiertas en cada fachada. En la época barroca el exterior sufrió serios cambios, como la apertura de una puerta en el centro del ábside mayor, vuelta a cerrar en las restauraciones decimonónicas, que tendieron a conferir al edificio su aspecto original. Bajo la iglesia se han hallado los restos de una mansión (o una casa señorial) que pueden fecharse entre los siglos III y V, cuyas estancias presentan paredes con frescos polícromos y suelos de mosaico.

it.name: Chiesa di San Nicolò lo Regale

en.name: Mosque and Minaret of the Mechouar (Citadel)
names: Mosque and Minaret of the Mechouar
description:
The old citadel of Mechouar, against the southern wall of the city, was built by Yaghmoracen (633-681 / 1235-1282) and served as an Almohad, Zyanid and later Turkish residence. At Mechouar (place of the council, site of government), this square and fortified complex remains today. An integral part of the historic centre of Tagrart, the Mechouar, according to legend, designates the precise place chosen by the Almoravid ibn Tachfin to pitch his tent in 1079, while he prepared to besiege the old town of Agadir, later called Tlemcen.  
  
There are mostly only ramparts left, and the mosque inside, completed in 718 / 1318 by Abu Hammou Moussa I. The hall of the oratory, with no courtyard, performed various functions; it served as an annex to the military hospital and as a Catholic chapel during the colonial period. The minaret has retained its proportions, as well as its decoration on all four sides: panels with carved columns and sets of arches on a mosaic background of glazed tiles.

fr.name: Le Méchouar
description:
La vieille citadelle du Méchouar, accolée au mur d’enceinte méridional de la ville, fut édifiée par Yaghmoracen (633-681/ 1235-1282) et servit de résidence almohade, zyanide et plus tard turque. Aujourd’hui, il reste cet ensemble carré et fortifié, “Méchouar” signifiant “lieu du Conseil”, c’est-à-dire là où le pouvoir siégeait pour gouverner. Partie intégrante du centre historique de Tagrart, le Méchouar, selon la légende, désignerait l’endroit précis choisi par l’Almoravide ibn Tachfin pour planter sa tente alors que, en 1079, il s’apprêtait à assiéger la vieille ville d’Agadir devenue Tlemcen.  
  
Il n’en reste pratiquement que les remparts, ainsi que, à l’intérieur, la mosquée terminée en 718/1318 par Abou Hammou Moussa Ier. La salle de l’oratoire, sans cour, a rempli diverses fonctions ; elle a notamment servi d’annexe à l’hôpital militaire et de chapelle catholique durant la période coloniale. Le minaret a conservé ses proportions, ainsi que son décor sur les quatre faces : des panneaux à colonnettes avec un ensemble d’arcatures sur fond de mosaïque de carreaux de faïence.

en.name: Uşak Rug with bird
description: Bird rugs are named for the S‒shaped stylised bird motifs arranged in vertical and horizontal rows in the centre field. This is a subgroup of rugs called white ground Ottoman rugs. The other types of white ground rugs are scorpion and *çintamani* rugs. The most popular ones are the bird rugs. Generally, the origin of this type is Uşak, however, research has found that many of these rugs were produced in Selendi in Manisa city. The rugs first appear in Western paintings in the 16th century and were probably not woven after the 18th century.
keywords: West Anatolia; Uşak rug with bird
materials: Natural wool coloured with natural dyes; Gördes knot; symmetrical knot
tags: Natural wool coloured with natural dyes
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

en.name: *Divine Wisdom hovering over Human Wisdom*
description: The scene celebrates Divine Wisdom through bold perspective and the supernatural light around the figures.
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: *La Sapienza Divina che sovrasta la Sapienza umana*
description: La scena pittorica dipinta nella volta centrale della sala maggiore, esalta la figura della Sapienza divina  che appare  in uno sfondato luminosissimo, alla sommità di una teoria di  figure  arditamente scorciate che si dirigono verso di lei o stanno in atteggiamento ammirativo. L’uso sapiente della luce, che trasmette una fortissima tensione al soprannaturale e un’evidente tensione all’infinito,  attira anche il riguardante nella dimensione quasi astratta del cielo. Ivi la personificazione della Divina Sapienza è avvolta da una luce abbagliante, con un effetto di ampliamento illusorio dello spazio reale nella dimensione celeste e metafisica.
place: Biblioteca, S. Michele in Bosco, Bologna (seconda sala)

en.name: Taoujout
description: The layout of the houses, the form of housing as well as the architectural techniques adopted in Taoujout are similar to those in Tamezret. The village is perched on a hillock, the highest point of which has been reserved for the mosque, whose minaret can be seen from afar, and includes the remains of an ancient *qsar*, meaning here a fortified site, dominating the valleys and the plateau. However in Taoujout, there are no ethnically divided neighbourhoods: small streets climb up to the summit and serve houses which back onto the sides of the mountain. These houses are built of stone bonded with plaster, comprising outbuildings and living spaces laid out around an open-roofed courtyard. Often, one or more rooms have been excavated, linking this type of house to the group of houses which are partly or fully cave-like in this part of south Tunisia.

es.name: Tauyut
description: La ordenación del hábitat, la forma de las viviendas, así como las técnicas arquitectónicas adoptadas en Tauyut son muy parecidas a las que ya se han mencionado en Tamezret. Se trata de una aldea posada sobre un cerro, que reserva la parte más alta a la mezquita, visible desde la lejanía gracias a su alminar y a las ruinas de un antiguo *ksar*, término que designa aquí a un lugar fortificado que domina los valles y la meseta. Sin embargo, en Tauyut es un punto de división étnica de diferentes barrios, sus callejuelas trepan hasta la cima y comunican las viviendas adosadas a la ladera de la montaña. Estas viviendas están construidas con piedra aparejada con yeso, y comprenden dependencias y habitaciones organizadas alrededor de un patio abierto. Frecuentemente tienen una o dos piezas excavadas y es esto lo que liga este tipo de vivienda al tipo de hábitat parcial o totalmente troglodita de esta parte del sur de Túnez.

fr.name: Taoujout
description: L’ordonnance de l’habitat, la forme de  l’habitation ainsi que les techniques architecturales  adoptées à Taoujout sont semblables  à celles notées à Tamezret. Il s’agit  d’un village juché sur un mamelon, réservant  le point culminant à la mosquée,  visible de loin par son minaret, et aux vestiges  d’un ancien ksar, terme qui désigne  ici un lieu fortifié, dominant les vallées et  le plateau. Mais à Taoujout, point de division  ethnique des quartiers: des ruelles  grimpent jusqu’au sommet et desservent  des habitations adossées au flanc de la  montagne. Ces demeures sont construites  en pierre liée avec du plâtre, comprenant  des communs et des chambres d’habitation  organisés autour d’une cour à ciel  ouvert. Une pièce ou plus est souvent  excavée, ce qui rattache ce type de maison à l’ensemble de l’habitat partiellement  ou totalement troglodytique de  cette partie du Sud tunisien.

en.name: Castle
description:
The Mediaeval castle is at the heart of Bragança, as it has been for over 700 years. It has undergone successive phases of construction, the most important being that which took place in the mid-15th century, even though it was a continuation of those ordered by D. João I. The *Livro das Fortalezas* by Duarte D’Armas, shows what the castle and settlement were like in the time of D. Manuel I.  
The upper part of the castle was the strongest and was adapted as living quarters for the *alcaide* and the dukes when they made their rare visits to their dukedom. The first work must date back to the reign of D. Sancho I, and further work was done during the reign of D. Afonso III. To the side was the centre of the city, the oldest part with narrow streets that formed a radiating network marked by a street joining the two gateways. The Church of Santa Maria stands inside the fortress proper, immediately abutting the cistern with, on the upper floor, the council chamber or *domus municipalis* with pierced rounded arches.  
The large tower of the keep, 30 m. high and 16 m. at the base seems to have been built between 1409 and 1449, and remains much the same today: dominating and gigantic. There are large rooms on the upper floors and a terrace with projecting towers at the corners. The keep is linked to the first enclosure by passages around the five-sided castle, with straight *curtain walls* with forward cubes or low, semicircular towers with embrasures to allow sweeping fire with primitive firearms.  
The remodelled, high Princess Tower that existed in 1507, is also important, standing well above the parapet and prepared for living quarters when not required for military purposes.  
The walls of the town occupied the remainder of the hillock, significantly increasing available defended space in the Mediaeval tradition. The wall is high, wide and surmounted by battlements with irregularly placed towers that protected the 2-m.-wide parapet.

en.name: 'Ethnographic Exhibition' [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
short_description: Colonel Le Clerc organized an ethnographic gallery inside his own museum of artillery for the International Exhibition of Paris in 1878. He arranged 72 examples of warriors coming from almost every part of the world in a three-room exhibit. These characters were modelled from actual examples and resembled Arabic, Australian, African and Indian people with costumes and features. The exhibition paid great attention to facial renderings and the physical appearance of the warriors.
keywords: International exhibition; Exposition universelle de Paris; international exposition; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; war; ethnography; ethnographic exhibition; book; magazine
partner: MIBACT | National Central Library of Rome

en.name: *Alexander Karatheodori Pasha (1833–1906)*
short_description: Portrait of Alexander Karatheodori Pasha. He was born in 1833 in the Greek quarter, Phanar, in Constantinople and served as leading diplomat (Premier Plénipotentiaire) of the Ottoman Empire at the 1878 Congress of Berlin. With the consent of the Ottoman government, Austro-Hungarian troops occupied Bosnia-Herzegovina.
keywords: Alexander Karatheodori Pasha;Congress of Berlin; Bosnia

ar.name: خوذة توربان
description: إن الخوذات من هذا النوع كان تدعى عادة بخوذ التوربان بسبب شكلها الفقاعي. والوعاء العريض للخوذة تم تشكيله بالطرق من صفيحة وحيدة من الفولاذ وتشكيل رأس مستدق متصل بشكل منفصل في الأعلى. والوعاء يحتفظ بعدة قطع مثقبة من أجل وصل الدرع المصنوع من الزرد والتي تحمي العنق.  تماما أعلى الفتحة المطابقة / الموصلة للعينين هناك بقية من نصل منزلق وقوسه / قطعة تثبيته وهي الآن مفقودة. وفوق وأسفل العصابة العريضة للأخاديد المحززة في مركز الوعاء يوجد عصابات نقش بسطح داخلي مطعم بالفضة بالخط النقشي على أرضية ملتفة ويقول النص جزئيا : المجد الدائم والرخاء للسلطان . ويوجد حفر فوق محجر العين اليسرى هو علامة / دمغة للترسانة العثمانية مما يعني أن الخوذة قد أخذت لتركيا كغنيمة.
dates: أواخر القرن التاسع الهجري / أواخر القرن الخامس عشر الميلا دي
keywords: درع ، قطع عسكرية ، مشغولة معدنية ، فضة ، فولاذ ، تطعيم ، نقش ، تخطيط
