en.name: Karatay Madrasa.
description:
Karatay Madrasa was built on a rectangular area measuring approximately 31.50 m x 26.50 m and oriented east to west. All the rooms are arranged around a dome-covered courtyard. The ruined students' cells on the north and south sides were rebuilt in the 1970s. The winter classroom in the northwest corner, as well as the rooms in the north and south corners of the east wing are in ruins  
The entrance to the *madrasa* is at the south end of the east side. Contrary to custom, the portal is not in the middle of the wall, and its form and decoration differ from other portals of this period.  
The courtyard at the centre of the building is covered by a dome. In the centre of the dome, a 5-m wide opening has been left to provide light and air. Below this opening, in the middle of the covered courtyard, is a square pool. Centrally placed at the west side of the courtyard is the main classroom, i.e. the *iwan*, and to either side of it are single winter classrooms. The classroom to the north of the *iwan* is in ruins, while the other one was converted into a tomb for Celaleddin \[Jalal al-Din\] Karatay, who built the *madrasa*. The *iwan* has a barrel vault, while the tomb has a dome. The students' cells situated north and south of the courtyard are also barrel-vaulted. The rooms on the entrance side of the *madrasa* are ruined.  
The east side of the *madrasa* where the entrance is located is made of cut stone, while the other walls are made of rubble stone. Bricks have been used in the upper sections of the walls, in the dome's zone of transition and in the vaults.  
In the *madrasa*, decoration can be seen to this day on the portal, the walls of the rooms facing the courtyard, the dome of the courtyard and the main *iwan*. The ornament on the portal consists of inscriptions and geometric and floral decoration executed in relief on marble. In addition, above and on both sides of the conch, the portal is decorated with interlacing geometric bands of grey and white marble. The decoration with swastika motifs on the panels flanking the portal is interesting. On the walls of the courtyard, its dome, and the main *iwan* there are both decorative tiles and tile mosaic. The traces which remain show that the main *iwan* and the lower part of the courtyard walls down to floor level were covered with hexagonal turquoise tiles. The tympana of the doorways and windows facing the courtyard, the upper part of the walls, the fan-shaped pendentives supporting the courtyard dome, the dome itself and the vault of the *iwan* have decoration in tile mosaic including inscriptions and floral and geometric motifs. The *iwan* is also adorned with relief-decorated tiles. The dome of the winter classroom which was converted into a tomb-chamber features unglazed bricks arranged in a herringbone pattern.

This *madrasa*'s courtyard is covered with a dome. The first examples of *madrasa*s were seen in the Transoxania and Khurasan regions and had a plan with an *iwan* in the middle of each side and other smaller rooms in between. The same layout is also observed in Anatolia where some examples have their courtyards covered with a dome or vault, which in addition has a cupola on the top providing light or ventilation.
artist: Celaleddin [Jalal al-Din] Karatay bin Abdullah, vizier of İzzeddin keykavus [‘Izz al-Din Kay Qawus] II.
keywords: Konya; museum; Seljuq architecture; education; madrasa; tiles; tile mosaic; floral decoration; geometric decoration; Celaleddin [Jalal al-Din] Karatay.

es.name: Madrasa de Karatay.
description:
La madrasa de Karatay se construyó sobre un área rectangular de aproximadamente 31,50 × 26,50 m y está orientada de este a oeste. Todas las salas están dispuestas alrededor de un patio cubierto por una cúpula. Las celdas en ruina de los estudiantes, al norte y al sur, se reconstruyeron en la década de 1970. El aula de invierno de la esquina noroeste y las salas de los ángulos norte y sur del ala oriental están en ruinas. La entrada a la madrasa se encuentra en el extremo sur de la cara este. A diferencia de lo habitual, la puerta no se abre en la mitad de la pared, y su forma y decoración difieren de las de otros portales del mismo periodo.  
El patio central del edificio está cubierto por una cúpula, en cuyo centro se dejó una abertura de cinco metros para permitir la entrada de aire y luz. Bajo esta abertura, en medio del patio cubierto, hay un estanque cuadrado. En el centro del lateral oeste del patio está el aula principal o *iwan*, flanqueada por dos aulas de invierno. El aula al norte del *iwan* está en ruinas y la otra se transformó en la tumba de Celaleddin Karatay, quien ordenó construir la madrasa. El *iwan* presenta una bóveda de cañón y la tumba está cubierta por una cúpula. Las celdas de los estudiantes situadas al norte y al sur del patio también tienen bóvedas de cañón. Las salas que están en el lado de la entrada de la madrasa están en ruinas.  
El lateral oriental de la madrasa, en el que se encuentra la entrada, está construido con piedra labrada, mientras que el resto de los muros son de piedra sin labrar. En la parte superior de las paredes, en la zona de transición a la cúpula y en las bóvedas se usaron ladrillos.  
Se conserva la decoración de la entrada de la madrasa, de los muros de las salas situadas frente al patio, de la cúpula y del *iwan* principal. La ornamentación del portal consta de inscripciones y decoración geométrica y floral en relieve sobre mármol. Además, encima y a los lados del arco, la puerta está decorada con bandas geométricas entrelazadas en mármol gris y blanco. Resulta interesante la decoración con esvásticas de los paneles que rodean la entrada. En las paredes del patio, la cúpula y el *iwan* principal hay azulejos decorativos y mosaicos de azulejo. Los vestigios que aún quedan en el edificio demuestran que el *iwan* principal y la parte baja de los muros del patio estuvieron cubiertos con azulejos hexagonales de color turquesa. Los tímpanos de las puertas y las ventanas que dan al patio, la parte superior de los muros, las pechinas en abanico que sostienen la cúpula del patio, la cúpula y la bóveda del *iwan* están decorados con mosaicos de azulejos, en los que aparecen motivos geométricos y florales e inscripciones. También el *iwan* está adornado con azulejos en relieve. La cúpula del aula de invierno que se transformó en cámara funeraria se construyó con ladrillos sin vidriar dispuestos en espiga.

Los primeros ejemplos de madrasas se encuentran en las regiones de Transoxiana y Jurasán, y poseen un *iwan* en mitad de cada lado y otras salas pequeñas entre medias. El mismo diseño se observa en Anatolia, donde los patios de algunas madrasas están cubiertos por una bóveda, que además tiene una cúpula en lo alto para proporcionar luz o ventilación. En el caso de esta madrasa, el patio está cubierto con una cúpula.
artist: Celaleddin Karatay bin Abdullah, visir de İzzeddin Keykavus II.
keywords: Konya; museo; arquitectura selyúquí; educación; madrasa; azulejos; mosaico de azulejos; decoración floral; decoración geométrica; Celaleddin Karatay.

fr.name: Madrasa Karatay.
description:
La *madrasa* Karatay occupe un plan rectangulaire de 31,5 x 26,5 m environ, orienté est-ouest. Toutes les salles sont disposées autour d'une cour surmontée d'une coupole. Les cellules jadis en ruine des étudiants au nord et au sud ont été reconstruites dans les années 1970. La salle de cours d'hiver à l'angle nord-ouest ainsi que les salles des angles nord et sud de l'aile orientale sont en ruine.  
L'entrée se fait par l'extrémité sud du côté est. Contrairement à la coutume, le portail ne se trouve pas au milieu du mur et sa forme comme sa décoration diffèrent de ceux des autres portails de la période.  
Au centre de la coupole de la cour centrale, une ouverture de 5 m de diamètre a été ménagée pour la circulation de l'air et de la lumière. Juste en dessous, au milieu donc de la cour, se trouve un bassin carré. Au centre du côté ouest se trouve la salle de cours, c'est-à-dire l'*iwan*, flanquée de deux salle de cours pour l'hiver. Celle au nord de l'*iwan* est en ruine, tandis que l'autre a été transformée en tombeau pour Celaleddin \[Djalal al-Din\] Karatay, constructeur de la *madrasa*. L'*iwan* est couvert d'une voûte en berceau, le tombeau d'une coupole. Les cellules d'étudiants situées au nord et au sud de la cour sont également à voûte en berceau. Les salles du côté de l'entrée sont en ruine. Le côté est de la *madrasa* – celui de l'entrée — est construit en pierres de taille, les autres sont en moellons. Des briques ont été utilisées pour les parties supérieures des murs, la base de la coupole et les voûtes.  
Le décor du portail, des murs des salles donnant sur la cour, de la coupole de celle-ci et de l'*iwan* principal a subsisté. L'ornementation du portail consiste en inscriptions, et en une décoration géométrique et florale sculptée en relief dans le marbre. Par ailleurs, au-dessus et de chaque côté de son arc, figurent des bandeaux géométriques entrelacés en marbre gris et blanc. La décoration à swastikas des panneaux latéraux de la porte est intéressante. Sur les murs de la cour, dans la coupole et l'*iwan* principal se trouvent des carreaux décoratifs et des mosaïques de carreaux. Les traces qui en restent montrent que l'*iwan* principal et la partie inférieure des murs de la cour jusqu'au sol étaient recouverts de carreaux hexagonaux de couleur turquoise. Le tympan des portes et des fenêtres face à la cour, la partie supérieure des murs, les pendentifs en éventails sous la coupole de la cour, la coupole elle-même et la voûte de l'*iwan* présentent un décor en mosaïque à inscriptions et motifs géométriques et floraux. L'*iwan* est également orné de carreaux en relief. La coupole de la salle de cours d'hiver, transformée en tombeau, est en briques non vernies posées en chevrons.

Cette cour de *madrasa* est couverte d’un dôme. Les premiers exemples de *madrasa* viennent des régions de la Transoxiane et du Khorassan ; elles étaient construites selon un plan avec, au milieu de chaque côté, un *iwan* flanqué de pièces plus petites. Le même schéma s’observe en Anatolie où dans certains exemples les cours sont couvertes d’un dôme ou de voûtes, surmontés d’une coupole procurant de la lumière et une ventilation.
artist: Celaleddin [Djalal al-Din] Karatay bin Abdullah, vizir de Azzeddin Keykavus [‘Izz al-Din Kay Qawus] II.
keywords: Konya ; musée ; architecture seldjoukide ; éducation ; madrasa ; carreaux ; mosaïque de carreaux ; décoration florale ; décoration géométrique ; Celaddin [Djalal al-Din] Karatay

tr.name: Karatay Medresesi.
description:
Doğu-batı doğrultusunda, yaklaşık 31.50x26.50 metre ölçülerinde dikdörtgen bir alan üzerine inşa edilmiştir. Mekanlar, bir kubbe ile örtülü bir avlunun çevresine yerleştirilmiştir. Kuzey ve güney kanadındaki öğrenci hücreleri, yıkıldıkları için 1970'li yıllarda yeniden inşa edilmişlerdir. Kuzeybatı köşesindeki kışlık dershane mekanı ile doğu kanadının güney ve kuzey köşelerinde yer alan mekanlar ise günümüzde de yıkık durumdadır.  
  
Medresenin girişi doğu cephesinin güney ucundadır. Alışılmışın dışında, cepheyi ortalamayan taçkapı, formu ve süslemeleri bakımından da, döneminin diğer taçkapı örneklerinden ayrılmaktadır.  
  
Ortada yer alan avlu bir kubbe ile örtülüdür. Kubbenin ortasında, ışık ve havalandırma için, 5.00m çapında bir açıklık bırakılmıştır. Açıklığın altında, avlunun ortasına yerleştirilmiş kare şekilli bir havuz vardır. Avlunun batı kenarının ortasında ana eyvan (dershane eyvanı) ve bunun iki yanına yerleştirilmiş birer kışlık dershane mekanı yer almaktadır. Eyvanın kuzeyindeki dershane yıkılmıştır. Diğer dershane mekanı ise, medreseyi inşa ettiren Celaleddin Karatay için türbe olarak düzenlenmiştir. Eyvan beşik tonozla; türbe ise, kubbe ile örtülüdür. Avlunun kuzey ve güneyinde sıralanan öğrenci hücreleri de beşik tonozla örtülüdür. Medresenin giriş kanadındaki mekanlar yıkıktır.  
  
Medrese girişinin bulunduğu doğu duvarı kesme taşlarla; diğer duvarlar ise, moloz taşlarla inşa edilmiştir. Duvarların üst kesimleri ve kubbe geçişleri ile kubbe ve tonozların inşaatında tuğla kullanılmıştır.  
  
Medresede, günümüze ulaşabilmiş süslemeler taçkapı, mekanların avluya bakan cepheleri, avlu kubbesi ve ana eyvanda görülmektedir. Taçkapıdaki süslemeler, mermer üzerine, kabartma tekniği ile yapılmış geometrik, bitkisel ve yazı örneklerinden oluşmaktadır. Ayrıca kavsaranın iki yanında ve üst kesiminde, gri ve beyaz renkte mermer ile yapılmış geçmeli geometrik süsleme vardır. Taçkapı yan kanatlarında, panolar içinde yer alan gamalı haçtan geliştirilmiş süslemeler ilginçtir. Mekanların avluya bakan cephelerinde, avlu kubbesinde ve ana eyvanda çini ve çini mozaik süslemeler vardır. Günümüze kalan izlerden, ana eyvan ve avlu duvarlarının alt kesimlerinin, zemine kadar altıgen şekilli firuze renkli çini plakalarla kaplı olduğu anlaşılmaktadır. Avluya bakan kapı ve pencere alınlıkları, duvarların üst kesimi, avlu kubbesine geçişi sağlayan yelpaze pandantifler, avlu kubbesi ve eyvan tonozunda yer alan bitkisel, geometrik ve yazı örneklerinden oluşan süslemeler ise çini mozaik tekniği ile oluşturulmuştur. Eyvanda kabartma çinilerle yapılmış süslemeler de vardır. Türbe olarak düzenlenmiş kışlık dershanenin kubbe örgüsünde, sırsız tuğlalarla balık kılçığı şeklinde dekoratif bir görünüm oluşturulmuştur.  
  
Yapı 1955'den beri çini Eserleri Müzesi'dir ve Türkiye eserlerinin bir kısmı bu müzeden seçilmiştir.

Avlusunun üzeri bir kubbe ile örtülüdür. İlk örnekleri Anadolu dışında, Horasan ve Maveraünnehir Bölgesi'nde görülen medreseler, üzeri açık bir avlunun her bir kenarının ortasına yerleştirilmiş birer eyvan ve bu eyvanlar arasındaki küçük mekânlardan oluşmaktaydı. Aynı plan şeması Anadolu'da da uygulanmasına karşın, bazı örneklerde avlunun kubbe veya tonozlarla örtülü olduğu görülmektedir. Bu örneklerde avluyu örten kubbe ya da tonozun tepesinde, ışık ve havalandırma amaçlı bir açıklık bırakıldığı görülmektedir.
keywords: Konya; Müze; Selçuklu mimarisi; Eğitim; Medrese; Çini; Çini-mozaik; bitkisel bezeme; geometrik bezeme; Celaleddin Karatay

de.name: Hochaltar und östliche Seitenaltäre
description: Der Hochaltar ist zusammen mit zwei Nebenaltären als kulissenartige  Schauwand über die ganze Breite des flachen Chorschlusses angelegt und bildet damit einen prachtvollen Prospekt und Raumabschluss. Die von Säulen gegliederte Schauwand bezieht die drei Altarbilder sowie zwei große Standfiguren mit ein und wird zudem von einem aufragenden Auszug über dem Hochaltar mit Stuckgloriole der heiligen Dreifaltigkeit überhöht.
artist: Johann Perger (1729-1774, Bildhauerarbeiten) und Johann Joseph Karl Henrici (1737-1823, Altargemälde)

en.name: High altar and eastern side altars
description: The high altar together with the two side altars, are arranged as a coulisse-like ornamental screen extending across the whole width of the flat choir termination, thus forming a magnificent concluding prospect. The ornamental screen, structured by columns, includes three altarpieces as well as two large statues and is surmounted by a protruding altar crown above the high altar with a stucco glory of the Holy Trinity.
artist: Johann Perger (1729–1774); Johann Joseph Karl Henrici (1737–1823)

cs.name: Zahradní průčelí
description: S přestavbou zámku byla projektována i zahrada. Francouzský architekt Carbonier zde působil v letech 1714–15. Zámecké průčelí se do zahrady otevíralo terasou s trojramenným schodištěm a sochami, které dekorovaly i zahradu. Dnes jsou umístěny do nik stereotomní fasády s lineární ostrou profilací prvků. Osový parter byl lemován dvojitými alejemi, kolem zámku byl vodní příkop. Zahrada s oranžerií byla považována za jednu z nejkrásnějších v zemi, místní zahradník Hatzl byl povolán na dvůr Marie Terezie jako správce zahrad Schönbrunnu. R. 1784 zde startoval první balón na Moravě.

en.name: Garden frontage
description: The garden was designed as part of the chateau reconstruction. The French architect, Charbonier, worked on the site in 1714–15. The chateau frontage opened onto the garden through a terrace with a three-shouldered staircase with statues that also decorated the garden. Today they are found in the niches of the stereotomous frontage with sharp linear elements. The axis parterre was lined by double pathways and the chateau was encircled by a moat. The garden, with a conservatory, was considered one of the most beautiful in the country. The local gardener, Hatzl, was summoned to the court of Maria Theresa and put in charge of the Schönbrunn gardens in Vienna. The first hot-air balloon in Moravia was launched outside the Židlochovice Chateau in 1784.
artist: Ernst August Charbonnier (1677–1747 Hannover?), Ludwig Sebastian Kaltner

en.name: Pena Palace
description:
High up in the Sintra hills, where previously there stood the 16th-century Monastery of Nossa Senhora da Pena, D. Fernando II built his legendary palace. This has since become the symbol of the king’s personality and the defining image of the spirit of Romanticism that was prevalent at that time.  
After purchasing the convent in 1838, the king had simply intended to repair the original building, but he ended up building a fortified palace that, in its first phase, had no overall guiding plan. However, roughly two years later, “His Majesty”, decided, “that the Convent should be transformed into a fortified palace, following the mixed Arabian, or Manueline, style of its origins”.  
In 1842, after building strong outside walls crowned by an elegant arcade drawn straight from a neo-Moorish textbook, the king ordered the chapel yard to be enlarged. The area that is now referred to as the queen’s terrace was made more extensive by constructing “elegant arcades” in the Arabian style in order to allow for the formation of loggias.  
The entrance gate, which is immediately followed by a drawbridge, provides some information on the symbolism that underlines its function as an “antechamber”.  
This chamber was to prepare the visitor for an understanding of the dreamlike (or perhaps real) delirium of the portico, an allegory of the creation of the world, which is sited a little further up the hill in the noble façade of the “new palace”.  
The overall project was the work of the engineer Ludwige Eschwege, but the king significantly changed the decoration, giving the impression that the German’s proposal had been cast aside.  
The portico known as the “Triton Arch” or the “allegory of the creation of the world” displays heavy symbolism connected to life itself, whether this is understood in the physical or spiritual sense. This leads to the arcaded courtyard, displaying in its passageway, together with much exoticism, “an elegant ceiling of Arabian taste, imitating natural stalactites”.  
On part of the façade overlooking the courtyard is the famous window inspired by that found on the outer wall of the chapter house at the Convento de Cristo (Tomar). This window was certainly designed by D. Fernando and can now be considered as representing the very birth of the neo-Manueline style.  
D. Fernando was not content simply to transpose this style to the Pena Palace, but instead produced an amalgam of Oriental, Moorish, Indian and maritime features, resulting in a compositional irregularity that is highly gratifying for those with a Romantic spirit.  
The interior decoration of the palace seems to have been carried out without any specific programme. That said, the fact remains that, at that time, the prevailing fashion was for decorators to effect a contrast between the styles used in different compartments, and such eclecticism provided a vast range of options, even though it was always guided by a taste for comfort.  
It was not by mere chance that D. Fernando’s palace appeared in its present position crowning the rocks of Pena, and its emergence here has in fact to be understood in a much broader context.

es.name: Palacio da Pena
description:
En lo alto de la sierra de Sintra, donde se encontraba el monasterio del siglo XVI de Nossa Senhora da Pena (Nuestra Señora de la Peña), D. Fernando II construyó su legendario palacio, emblema de la personalidad del rey y también del romanticismo vigente.  
Al comprarlo, en 1838, el monarca solo pretendía reparar el convento, pero terminó por construir un palacio encastillado que, en una primera fase, no siguió ningún plan rector; con todo, cerca de dos años más tarde, Su Majestad resolvió “que el convento se transformase en palacio encastillado, siguiendo el estilo árabe mixto o *manuelino* que primitivamente tenía”.  
En 1842, el rey, después de construir fuertes paredones, coronados por una elegante arquería que se inscribía en un lenguaje neomorisco, mandó ensanchar la explanada de entrada de la capilla y, para que la ahora denominada Terraza de la Reina fuera más extensa, hizo levantar en el paramento “vistosas arcadas de estilo árabe”, de modo que se formaran galerías abiertas.  
En el portón de entrada, tras el que hay un puente levadizo, encontramos símbolos que subrayan su función de “antecámara” destinada a preparar al visitante para la comprensión del delirio, onírico o real, del pórtico alegórico de la creación del mundo, situado un poco más arriba, en la fachada noble del “palacio nuevo”.  
El proyecto de la obra fue dibujado, globalmente, por el ingeniero Ludwige Eschwege, pero el monarca alteró significativamente la decoración, y da la impresión de que la propuesta del alemán quedó al margen.  
El pórtico llamado del Tritón o de la “alegoría de la creación del mundo” presenta una simbología estrechamente ligada a la vida, ya se tome en el sentido físico o en el espiritual, y comunica con el patio de los Arcos a través de un pasadizo de gran exotismo y con “un elegante techo de gusto árabe, que imita estalactitas naturales”.  
En el alzado de la fachada que da a dicho patio está la famosa ventana inspirada en la de la sala capitular del convento de Cristo (Tomar), salida ciertamente del lápiz fernandino y que muy bien puede considerarse como la partida de nacimiento del neomanuelino.  
D. Fernando no se contentó con trasponer este estilo al palacio, sino que amalgamó elementos orientales, *moriscos*, indios y marítimos con una irregularidad compositiva muy gratificante para los espíritus románticos.  
Interiormente, la decoración de las diversas dependencias del palacio parece haberse llevado a cabo sin ninguna preocupación de orden programático, pero lo cierto es que por entonces estaba de moda el contraste entre los estilos utilizados en las diferentes estancias y el eclecticismo disponía de un amplio abanico de opciones, si bien siempre condicionado por la búsqueda de comodidad.  
El edificio de D. Fernando no apareció por simple casualidad sobre esta cima rocosa; hay que entender su construcción en un sentido mucho más amplio.

en.name: Panel of *azulejos* with a carpet composition
description:
Like many other examples, these *azulejos* testify to the affinity between textiles and *azulejos* in Portugal during the 17th century. Such was the case with the embroidered Arraiolos rugs made in the Alentejo region where the same sort of patterns and even palette can be recognised.  
This pattern was relatively common in the *azulejos* used in Portugal during the first half of the 17th century. Because this is a 2 x 2 composition, four *azulejos* are required to make a pattern that can be repeated to infinity. Use of this sort of *azulejos* was mainly in the lower areas of architecture to allow viewers to approach the decoration more directly. In it, we can perceive a cross-like composition that is achieved by a much-intertwined element with a dense blue background, at the centre of which is an acanthus leaf motif. This rope-like cross composition is placed against a yellow background; here, a distinctive eight-point motif, which has its origins in leather- or metalwork, can be traced by the presence of nail marks left in all four of its extremities. The beautiful frame that can be seen in one of its borders is known in Portuguese as *rendas* or lacework, inspired by actual works.  
Some studies have shown that prints of these lace motifs could be made by the immersion of real lace in the pigments, which were then juxtaposed in the *azulejos*, or that these were painted using similar gestures as those used to make the real lace. This has not been the case for the motifs that decorate these *azulejos*, but nevertheless the elegance of this decoration gives a new and more regal understanding to this pattern type.
keywords: *faience*; *azulejos*; pattern; 17th century

en.name: Bond of 100 francs issued by the Caisse Générale de Secours et de Bienfaisance Israélite de Tunis, in order to raise funds for the construction of a new synagogue in Tunis, and bought by Leone Moreno
short_description:
The construction of the Great Synagogue in Tunis had a long and complicated history. In 1883, the Bey granted a plot of land on which to build the temple to the Italian Jewish physician and president of the Alliance Israélite Universelle of Tunis, Giacomo Castelnuovo. However, the synagogue was ultimately built on a different lot, acquired thanks to a private donation. In the first years of the 20th century, different projects were discussed. The synagogue was finally built in the 1930s.  
  
Leone Moreno (Tunis 1852 – Tunis 1950) was a successful Italian entrepreneur. He belonged to a Jewish family that had migrated from Livorno (Tuscany) to Tunis around 1830. He was awarded honours both by the Italian King (Cavaliere dell’Ordine della Corona d’Italia) and by the Bey of Tunis (Nichan Iftikhar).

ar.name: سجادة
description:
هذه السجاده ذو الوجهين مزخرفة بأشكال نباتية و هندسية وبآيات القرآن والشعر باللغتين الفارسية والعربية. يتميز السجاد القاجاري بكثير من الزخارف المصورة ،أيضاً أتقن النسّاجون من مدينة كرمان الإيرانية تقنية نادرة تتمثل في صناعة السجاد ذات الوجهين .  
  
تماما كوجهين مختلفين لعملة واحدة، تعرض السجاده موضوعين مُختلفين؛ الجنة والدنيا. بينما يصور أحد الجانبين حديقة مُصوّرة مع أشكال من الأزهار والحمام والطواويس ترمز إلى الجنة، يظهر على الجانب الآخر ميدالية في المنتصف مع نبات الفاوانيا وأزهار الزنبق واللوتس.  
  
لطالما اشتهر السجاد الفارسي بسبب ما يتضمّن سياقه الزخرفي من موضوعات سياسية واجتماعية مسجلة داخل الخيوط المنسوجه للسجاد كوسيلة لنقل القصص والحكايات. وما تزال سمة صناعة هذا السجاد قائمة حتى يومنا هذا باعتبارها " شهادة للهوية الثقافية " بالنسبة لإيران.
holder: متحف الشيخ فيصل بن قاسم ال ثاني
partner: متحف الشيخ فيصل بن قاسم ال ثاني

en.name: Qajar Double-sided Carpet
description:
Persian carpets have long stood out by including socio-political elements from local history within the thread as a story-telling motif woven into their fabric. This distinctive trait has become the Iranian carpet-making “cultural birth-certificate” still enduring today.  
  
While the style of this pictorial carpet characterizes the Qajar dynasty, this unique example was manufactured using a rare technique mastered in the town of Kerman, Iran. Like the flip sides of a coin, the carpet portrays two opposing scenarios: paradise and the universe, using floral and geometric patterns, Qur’anic verses, and poetry in Persian and Arabic. While one side depicts a lush garden with floral motifs, doves and peacocks, the other illustrates a central medallion with peonies, lilies and lotus flowers.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: Qajar; Double-sided Carpet; Kerman; Iran
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

en.name: *View of Jaffa*
description: Travel illustrations in the 19th century, with their images of life, history and topography, had a great influence over Orientalism. This engraving appeared in a publication about the history of Turkey. Jaffa was a very important port in East Mediterranean.
keywords: Egypt; Ottoman Empire; Haifa; War

en.name: Serra de Monchique
description: The Serra de Monchique, with its pastures always kept moist by the Atlantic breeze and its dense forests of corkoaks and chestnut trees, may be considered a special microclimate that is a source of incalculable wealth for the whole of the western region of the Algarve. This fact alone makes it easy to understand the significance and long history of its settlement. On its southern slopes, at the Spa of Caldas de Mochique, there is a thermal spring that has been popular since Roman times. The mountain ridges are crossed by an old road, in an area of much older settlements, surrounded by terraces and gardens, there stretches out before the visitor the present-day town of Monchique. On another ridge stands the ruins of the Islamic fortress of Alferce, which served as a watchtower controlling another mountain pass and marking the boundary of the district of Silves.

es.name: Sierra de Monchique
description: La sierra de Monchique, con sus pastos siempre humedecidos por las brisas atlánticas y los densos bosques de robles y castaños, puede considerarse un microclima de incalculable riqueza para todo el barlovento del Algarve. Se comprende así la razón y antigüedad de su poblamiento. En sus laderas meridionales, en la localidad de Termas de Monchique, brotan aguas termales a las que se acude desde el tiempo de los romanos. Al trasponer las cumbres por una vieja carretera, en un lugar de antiguo asentamiento y rodeada de apacibles caminos y jardines, se extiende hoy la villa de Monchique. En otra elevación, las ruinas de la fortaleza islámica de Alferce, con su papel de atalaya, controlaban otro paso de la sierra y delimitaban el término de Silves.

en.name: Sidi Bushwaisha Mosque
description:
The mosque, which has been attributed to Sidi Bushwaisha, the “man with the toupet”, is situated in the northern part of town, in front of Bab al-Jibli, the gate that leads to *suq*s seething with life. As his surname, Guardian of the Gate, *Shawush al-Bab*, suggests, Sidi Buchwaicha was probably the guardian of this strategic gate that would have been closed at nightfall. One is tempted to also consider him as the protector and defender of the gate, especially if one thinks of his mosque as a sort of *ribat*.  
This mosque limited itself to being a small prayer room flanked by a courtyard. It was enlarged in the 11th–12th/end of 17th century at the expense of its courtyard and of a partition oratory, endowing itself with a minaret and a beautiful facade. The prayer room is thus actually made-up of two linked but neatly distinct parts. The part built in the 11th/17th century, whilst imitating the older room in its use of columns and recycled capitals, is more elaborate; its *mihrab* is more imposing, and makes use of *faience* tiles as well as sculpted *kadhal*.  
The minaret offers a beautiful view of the Blacksmiths’ *suq* from above. Old engravings and postcards have enabled us to follow its evolution. Restoration work undertaken in 1964–1965 have returned it to its original form of two superimposed towers surmounted by a smooth skullcap-shaped lantern. Although constructed later, it falls in line with the pure architectural tradition of Ifriqiya. It is without doubt based and modelled on the minaret of the Great Mosque.  
The northern facade has been carefully elaborated. Adorned with wrought-iron windows with spiral features, *zlabiya*s, the facade is particularly distinct for the *kadhal* framing of its door and neighbouring windows. The small chain mouldings, the dentils, the three petal rosettes, the solar discs with rays that repeat and revert, all harmoniously combined, constitute a good mix of local architectural elements and Muradite novelty.  
Two niched inscriptions, within two sets of twin arches, surmount the entrance on either side. They reveal the date of the mosque’s extension in 1094/1683, and mention the five *murabitun*s who supported it as well as the master mason who executed the building work. He was Mohamed, son of the Master Mason Mohamed al-Kotti al-Ansari. This mention clearly demonstrates that the job of a mason, like many other professions, passed from father to son and from one generation to another. This conclusively explains the long-lasting nature of architectural traditions in Sfax.  
Restoration works uncovered in the southeast corner of the facade, the fountain (*sabil*), called by one, sucker (*sic*.), *massassa*. It is composed of a large vessel into which a leather tube is submerged; only the outer end of the tube is visible, and is placed at a man’s height. Those who were thirsty drank the water they required through sucking on the tube. Great religious and social importance was attached to these *sabil*s, whose purpose was to obtain divine mercy through quenching the thirsty.

es.name: Mezquita Sidi Buchwaicha
description:
La mezquita, que se atribuye a Sidi Buchwaicha (el hombre del mechón), está situada al norte de la ciudad, frente a la Bab el-Yibli, puerta que da acceso a los bulliciosos zocos. Tal y como lo sugiere su sobrenombre, “guardián de la puerta” (*chawash el-bab*), Sidi Buchwaicha era quizá el guardián de esta puerta estratégica que debía cerrarse a la caída de la noche. Puede ser también que se le llamara así porque fuera el defensor y protector de la puerta, sobre todos si consideramos su mezquita como una especie de *ribat*.  
Esta mezquita era únicamente una pequeña sala flanqueada por un patio. Fue ampliada entre los siglos XI-XII/f. XVII, en beneficio del patio y un oratorio mediano, y dotada de un alminar y una bella fachada. La sala de oración está formada actualmente por dos piezas comunicadas, pero claramente distintas. La del siglo XI/XVII, aunque imita la antigua sala, con columnas y capiteles reutilizados, es la más elaborada; su *mihrab* es más imponente porque utiliza, además del *kadhal* esculpido, los azulejos.  
El alminar ofrece una bella panorámica sobre los tejados del zoco de los Herreros. Unos grabados antiguos y tarjetas postales nos han permitido seguir su evolución. Las obras de restauración de 1964 a 1965 restituyeron su forma original, compuesta por dos torres superpuestas, coronadas por una lucernaria de calota lisa. Aunque tardío, se inscribe en la pura tradición arquitectónica ifriqí y es indudable que el alminar de la Mezquita Mayor le sirvió como modelo.  
La fachada norte está cuidadosamente elaborada. Adornada mediante ventanas de herrería con elementos en espiral (*zlabia*), se distingue sobre todo por los marcos de *kadhal* de la puerta y las ventanas que la flanquean. Las molduras en cadenas, los dentículos, las rosas de tres pétalos, los discos solares con rayos vueltos armoniosamente dispuestos constituyen una buena mezcla de elementos de la arquitectura local con las novedades muradíes. Dos inscripciones en nichos, en dos pequeñas arcadas geminadas, forman la culminación de la decoración de la entrada; en ellas se mencionan las obras de ampliación de la mezquita en 1094/1683 y se nombra a los cinco morabitos que posibilitaron las obras, así como al arquitecto que ejecutó el trabajo. Se trataba de Mohamed, hijo del maestro albañil Mohamed, que a su vez era hijo del arquitecto Mohamed el-Kutti el-Ansari. Esta mención demuestra claramente que el oficio de arquitecto, como muchos otros, pasaba de padres a hijos y de una generación a otra. Lo que explica, por otra parte, la perennidad de las tradiciones arquitectónicas en Sfax.  
Los trabajos de restauración han descubierto el ángulo sudeste de la fachada, en el que se sitúa la fuente de *sabil*, a la que se llama “el chupador” (*masasa*). Se trata de un recipiente que deja caer agua en un tubo de cobre del que, desde fuera, sólo puede verse una de las extremidades, situada a la altura de un hombre. Quien pase por allí y tenga sed podrá obtener toda el agua que necesite mediante aspiración. Desde el punto de vista religioso y social se atribuye una gran importancia a estos *sabil*s, cuyo principal objetivo era apagar la sed de los sedientos, gracias a la misericordia divina.

fr.name: Mosquée Sidi Bouchwaïcha
description:
La mosquée, qu’on attribue à Sidi Bouchwaïcha, l’homme au toupet, se situe au nord de la ville, en face de Bab el- Jibli, la porte qui donne accès à des souks grouillants. Comme le suggère son surnom de Gardien de la Porte, *Chaouch el- Bab*, Sidi Bouchwaïcha était peut-être le gardien de cette porte stratégique qui devait être fermée à la tombée de la nuit. On est tenté de le désigner, aussi, comme étant le défenseur et le protecteur de la porte, surtout si on considère sa mosquée comme une sorte de *ribat*.  
Cette mosquée se limitait à une petite salle de prière flanquée d’une cour. Elle s’est agrandie XIe-XIIe/f. XVIIe siècle au profit de cette cour et un oratoire mitoyen, tout en se dotant d’un minaret et d’une belle façade. La salle de prière est formée actuellement de deux parties communicantes, mais nettement distinctes. Celle du XIe/XVIIe siècle, quoique imitant l’ancienne salle dans l’utilisation de colonnes et de chapiteaux de réemploi, est plus élaborée; son *mihrab* est plus imposant, utilisant, en plus du kadhal sculpté, les carreaux de faïence.  
Le minaret offre une belle perspective du haut du souk des Forgerons. Les vieilles gravures et cartes postales nous ont permis de suivre son évolution. Les travaux de restauration de 1964-1965 lui ont restitué sa forme originelle en deux tours superposées surmontées d’un lanternon à calotte lisse. Quoique tardif, il s’inscrit dans la pure tradition architecturale ifriqiyenne. Le minaret de la Grande Mosquée lui a sans doute servi de modèle.  
La façade nord est soigneusement élaborée. Agrémentée par les fenêtres à ferronnerie en éléments spiralés, les *zlabia*s, elle se distingue surtout par les encadrements en *kadhal* de la porte et des fenêtres qui la flanquent. Les moulures en chaînettes, les denticules, les rosaces à trois pétales, les disques solaires à rayons retournés, harmonieusement agencés, constituent un bon mélange d’éléments d’architecture locale et de nouveautés mouradites. Deux inscriptions nichées, dans deux petites arcades géminées, surmontent de part et d’autre l’entrée. Elles font état de l’agrandissement de la mosquée en 1094/1683, mentionnent les cinq *mourabitoun* qui l’ont soutenue et le maître maçon qui a exécuté les travaux. Il s’agissait de Mohamed, fils du maître maçon Mohamed el-Kotti el-Ansari. Cette mention montre clairement que le métier de maçon, comme bien d’autres, passait du père au fils et d’une génération à une autre. Ce qui explique en définitive la pérennité des traditions architecturales à Sfax.  
Les travaux de restauration ont mis au jour, à l’angle sud-est de la façade, la fontaine du *sabil* qu’on appelait suçoir, *massassa*. Il s’agit d’une grande jarre dans laquelle trempe un tube en cuivre dont on ne voit à l’extérieur que l’extrémité placée à niveau d’homme. Celui qui avait soif obtenait l’eau dont il avait besoin par aspiration. On attachait sur le plan religieux et social une grande importance à ces *sabil*s, dont le but était d’obtenir, en désaltérant les assoiffés, la miséricorde divine.

ar.name: كنيسة القديس جوفاني داي ليبروزي ( وباء الجذام).
description:
بناء الكنيسة ذو شكل متميز؛ يتألف من ثلاثة أروقة، وثلاثة أعمدة قوية ذات زوايا متعددة، تحمل أربعة أقواس منحنية قليلا. الأروقة تتجه نحو الشرق، والمذبح مغلق بثلاثة محاريب، لها أعمدة صغيرة في الزوايا. نجد على يمين أحد هذه المحاريب وعلى تاج عمود زاويته زخرفة عربية بخط كوفي غير مقروء تآكل بفعل الزمن.  
تاريخ بناء هذه الكنيسة غير معروف لعدم وجود وثائق له. يقول السيد تومازو فاتزلو: (في القرن السادس عشر) كان قصراً للمسلمين، جعله النورمنديون مخيماً ينطلقون منه لاحتلال مدينة باليرمو أثناء محاصرتها عام (463/ 1071)، بعد خروج المسلمين منه. بعدئذ أمر روبرتو غويسكاردو وشقيق روجييرو ألتافيلا بتحويله إلى كنيسة، وقد بقي فيها آثار من القصر في بعض الجدران وأجزاء من الأرض وأشجار النخيل المحيطة به. وفي هذا البناء بعض التشابه مع الكنائس في مدينة مسينا المبنية بأمر النورمنديين من مثل استعمال الأعمدة للتقسيم الداخلي.  
أما مشفى الجذام فقد انشئ في وقت لاحق بين عام ؟(534-544/1140-1150).

اعتمادا على الرواية، فإن الكنيسة قد يرجع تأسيسها إلى روبير جيسكارد وأخيه روجي دي هوتفيل خلال حصار مدينة باليرمو عام 1071، فوق موقع كان يتواجد به حصن عربي؛ ومن الممكن أن نر بعض البقايا لهذا الأخير (أجزاء أسوار وبلاطات أرضية)، قرب الكنيسة. وفي الداخل، يقدم تاج عمود نقيشة عربية بأحرف كوفية تصعب حاليا قراءتها.
keywords: منشأة دينية.
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

en.name: San Giovanni dei Lebbrosi.
description: The church has distinct external lines and a basilica layout with three naves separated by three pairs of robust polygonal pillars supporting four slightly pointed arches. The naves proceed eastwards to the presbytery and its three apses with small corner columns. To the right there is a corner column whose capital bears an Arabic inscription in *kufic* script, now unfortunately too worn to be legible.

According to tradition, this church was founded by Robert Guiscard and his brother Roger of Altavilla (Ruggero I) during the siege of Palermo in 1071 on the site an existing Saracen castle, of which some remains (wall sections and fragments of flooring) can still be seen beside the church. Inside, the capital of a column bears an Arabic inscription in *kufic* characters, now illegible.
history:
A lack of documentary evidence makes it difficult to date the original construction. According to Tommaso Fazello (16th century), the church was founded by Robert Guiscard and his brother Roger d’Altavilla (Ruggero I) during the siege of Palermo in 1071, on the site of an earlier Saracen castle. Remains of this castle have survived, mainly sections of wall and fragments of flooring next to the church. It was surrounded by a palm grove, which the Normans used as an encampment from which to launch their final attack to take the city. In any case, the church would have been completed after the city had been conquered. The building has some peculiarities compared to other buildings in Palermo: it bears some similarities to the first churches built by the Normans around Messina, as well as some original features, such as the use of pillars in the naves.  
The leper colony from which it takes its name would have been added between 1140 and 1150.
keywords: religious architecture
partner: Regione Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

es.name: San Juan de los Leprosos.
description:
La iglesia presenta volúmenes exteriores bien definidos y una planta basilical de tres naves, separadas por tres parejas de robustos pilares de sección poligonal sobre los que se alzan cuatro arcadas de curvatura ligeramente apuntada. Las naves conducen, hacia el lado oriental, al presbiterio y a sus tres ábsides con pequeñas columnas angulares. A la derecha puede verse el capitel de una columna angular, con una inscripción árabe en caracteres cúficos, lamentablemente indescifrables por estar desgastados. A falta de documentos, resulta incierto datar la planta más antigua. Según Tommaso Fazello (siglo X / XVI), la iglesia fue fundada por Roberto el Guiscardo y su hermano Ruggero de Altavilla durante el asedio de Palermo en 1071, en el mismo lugar donde había un castillo sarraceno. De este se ven algunos restos, en su mayoría tramos de muro y fragmentos de pavimento, junto a la iglesia. Estaba rodeado por un palmeral que los normandos destinaron a campamento, desde el cual desencadenaron el ataque decisivo para expugnar la ciudad. En cualquier caso, parece probable que la construcción terminara una vez concluida la conquista. La iglesia muestra, con todo, algunas peculiaridades respecto a las otras realizaciones palermitanas: se observan ciertas afinidades con las primeras iglesias construidas por los normandos en el territorio de Messina y presenta algunos rasgos originales, como el uso de pilares en las naves.  
La leprosería que le da nombre debió de añadirseentre 1140 y 1150.

Según la tradición, la iglesia fue fundada por Roberto el Guiscardo y su hermano Ruggero de Altavilla durante el asedio de Palermo de 1071, en el mismo lugar donde había un castillo sarraceno. De este se ven algunos restos (tramos de muro y fragmentos de pavimento) junto a la iglesia. En el interior, el capitel de una columna presenta una inscripción árabe en caracteres cúficos, indescifrable.
keywords: arquitectura religiosa
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

fr.name: San Giovanni dei Lebbrosi.
description:
L'église, dont les volumes extérieurs sont nets, présente un plan basilical à trois nefs, séparées par trois paires de robustes piliers à section polygonale sur lesquels s'appuient quatre arcades légèrement en ogive. À l'est, les nefs conduisent au *presbyterium* qui se clôt sur trois absides à colonnettes d'angle. Sur la droite, on voit distinctement le chapiteau d'une colonne d'angle, avec inscription arabe en caractères coufiques, malheureusement indéchiffrables par suite de l'usure.  
  
Faute de documents, la datation de la première construction est incertaine. Selon Tommaso Fazello (XVIe siècle), l'église aurait été fondée par Robert Guiscard et par son frère Roger de Hauteville, durant le siège de Palerme en 1071, sur le site où s'élevait un château sarrasin. On peut voir des vestiges de ce dernier, essentiellement des pans de mur et des fragments de pavement, près de l'église ; il était entouré d'une palmeraie que les Normands aménagèrent en camp militaire d'où ils lancèrent leur attaque décisive, afin de s'emparer de la ville. L'église ne fut achevée qu'après la conquête définitive de la ville. L'édifice présente certaines particularités par rapport à d'autres réalisations palermitaines : on y relève des affinités avec les premières églises construites par les Normands sur le territoire de Messine, ainsi que des traits originaux, comme l'utilisation des piliers dans les nefs.  
  
La léproserie aurait été ajoutée entre 1140 et 1150.

À l'intérieur, le chapiteau d'une colonne présente une inscription arabe en caractères coufiques, désormais indéchiffrable.

it.name: San Giovanni dei Lebbrosi.
description: La chiesa, dai nitidi volumi esterni, presenta un impianto basilicale a tre navate, divise da tre coppie di robusti pilastri a sezione poligonale sui quali impostano quattro arcate dal sesto leggermente acuto. Le navate conducono, verso est, al presbiterio concluso da tre absidi con colonnine angolari. Sulla destra è visibile il capitello di una colonna angolare, con iscrizione araba a caratteri cufici, purtroppo indecifrabili perché abrasi. Incerta è la datazione del primo impianto in mancanza di documenti. Secondo Tommaso Fazello (XVI secolo) la chiesa sarebbe stata fondata da Roberto il Guiscardo e dal fratello Ruggero d'Altavilla durante l'assedio di Palermo del 1071, sullo stesso sito dove esisteva un castello saraceno. Di questo si vedono alcuni resti, perlopiù tratti di muro e frammenti di pavimentazione, accanto alla chiesa; era circondato da un palmeto che i normanni adibirono ad accampamento da cui sferrarono l'attacco decisivo per espugnare la città. La chiesa sarebbe stata comunque ultimata solo dopo la conquista definitiva della città. L'edificio mostra alcune singolarità rispetto alle altre realizzazioni palermitane: rivela alcune affinità con le prime chiese costruite dai normanni in territorio messinese e presenta alcuni caratteri originali, come l'uso dei pilastri nelle navate. Il lebbrosario sarebbe stato aggiunto tra il 1140 e il 1150.

en.name: Materials found in the Kamiros excavations in Rodi
names: Materiali provenienti dagli scavi di Kamiros a Rodi
short_description: Total view of materials chosen by Luigi Pernier, director of Archaeological School of Athens, from the excavation in Kamiros area (Rhodes) in 1912. Pernier sent his student Gian Giacomo Porro to the isle of Rhodes in order to explore this area and find a number of archaeological sites for the Italian Mission to concentrate its future excavations. Pernier decided to send part of the findings to the Prehistoric and Ethnographic Museum in Rome founded by Luigi Pigorini. These materials include mainly grave goods.

ar.name: لوح خشبي محفور
description: ربما كان هذا اللوح في الأساس يشكل جانبًا من أحد النُصُب التذكارية. ويزدان الوسط بزخارف على شكل ألواح مربعة ومستطيلة ومتعددة الأضلاع محفور عليها أشكال دائرية بها عناصر نباتية وزخارف حلزونية من الأرابيسك منظمة جميعها داخل إطار هندسي. ويحيط باللوح الأوسط كتابات بخط النسخ تشتمل على الآية 225 من سورة البقرة وحواشي حلزونية مزخرفة.

en.name: Carved wooden panel
description: This panel may originally have formed the side of a cenotaph. Its centre is decorated with square, rectangular and polygonal panels carved with vegetal roundels and arabesque scrolls and set into a geometric framework. *Naskhi* inscriptions giving verse 255 from *sura Al-Baqara* and scrolling friezes surround the central panel.
dates: Hegira early 7th century / AD early 13th century
keywords: Panel; naskhi; wood; carving; funerary object; inscription; calligraphy

ar.name: طبق
description: طبق كبير من البورسلين الأبيض عليه تزجيج بلون أزرق كوبالتي، في وسطه إطار دائري داخله كتابات، تحيط به أربع دوائر وضعت على مسافات متساوية وتضم نفس النص. توجد علامة من ستة أحرف داخل قاعدة الطبق بالخط الهونجزهاي محصورة داخل دائرة، يحدها خط مزدوج. في الميدالية الوسطى كتبت العبارة التالية: "سلم تسليما كثيرا كبيرا بفضلك ورحمتك يا أرحم الراحمين". أما في الميداليات المحيطة بها، فكتبت العبارة التالية: "لا فتى إلا علي لا سيف إلا ذو الفقرة [الفقار] وعلي هو الحق لا موت أصيب إلا بالأجل". وأما الكتابات حول حافة الطبق فهي كالتالي: "ناد عليا مظهر العجائب/ تجده عونا لك في النوائب/المعولي إلى الله حاجت/كل هم وغم سينجلي بنبوتك يا محمد وبولايتك يا علي يا علي يا علي/بحق ذي الملك والملكوت/ اعتصمت بذي العزة والقدرة والجبروت/ وتوكلنا على الذي لا ينام ولا يموت/دخلت في حرم الله وفي حفظ الله من شر البريت [البرية] أجمعين بحق حم بحق كهيعص وعسق لا حول ولا قوت [قوة] إلا بالله العلي العظيم صلى الله على المسطفى [المصطفى] محمد وآله أجمعين.

en.name: Dish
description:
Large white porcelain dish with cobalt blue glaze decorated with a central inscribed roundel surrounded by four evenly spaced roundels each filled with an identical inscription. The interior of the foot is a Hongzhi six-character mark withing a a double line roundel.  
In the central roundel: "Bestow numerous blessings and great honour upon him for You are the Most Merciful of those who show mercy." In the surrounding roundels, a repetition of: "There is no youth other than \`Ali There is no sword other than Zulficar And \`Ali is the Rightful Death will only strike at the appointed time."  
Around the rim: "In the name of God the Compassionate, the Merciful Call unto \`Ali the paragon of wonders, you shall find him of help in your misfortune. He who is relied upon \[to intercede\] before God for all needs All anguish and all sorrow shall disappear, through your Prophethood Oh Muhammad and through your Divine trusteeship, Oh \`Ali, Oh \`Ali, Oh \`Ali By the Divine Truth of The Absolute Sovereign of all things I take refuge in He Who has the glory, the might and the power And we put our trust in He Who slumbers and perishes not I take refuge in God's sanctuary, and in His protection from the evil of all beings By the truth of "ham", by the truth of "kahi\`us" and "\`asaq" There is neither power nor strength but in God, The Most High, The Supreme May the blessing of God be upon Muhammad Mustafa (the Chosen) and his family collectively."
keywords: Dish; China; Glaze

en.name: *The Lookouts*
short_description:
After his short, initial trip to Algeria in 1846 when he stayed at Blida, the artist returned in 1847 and 1848, staying in Constantine and Biskra. From then on Algeria became his primary source of inspiration, thanks to which he created these Algerian "impressions", as well as a number of paintings and drawings and two pieces of travel writing in 1857 and 1858. The emotions evoked by experience of such a different landscape fill the first account, *Une Année dans le Sahel* (1874), as well as the writer's admiration for the people, their simplicity and their attentiveness, their habits and their customs. He also deplores the Western urbanism which has already begun to destroy the country's authenticity.  
He also visited Egypt for the inauguration of the Suez Canal. He is one of the many artists who brought a degree of humanity back to Orientalist art.

fr.name: *Les guetteurs*
short_description: Après un premier bref voyage en Algérie en 1846 où il séjourne à Blida, il revient en 1847 et 1848 à Constantine et Biskra. L’Algérie demeurera dès lors sa première source d’inspiration et il tire de ces « impressions » algériennes, outre nombre d’œuvres peintes et dessinées, deux récits de voyage en 1857 et 1858. Dans le premier, *Une année dans le Sahel* (1874), il exprime toutes les émotions que lui procure le contact des paysages et d’une nature d’une diversité extrême, des personnages dont il apprécie la simplicité et observation attentivement les us et coutumes des habitants, déplorant que l’urbanisme occidental en détruise déjà l’authenticité. Il visitera l’Egypte à l’occasion de l’inauguration du canal de Suez. Il inaugure la longue lignée d’artistes qui restitueront sa dimension humaine à l’art orientaliste.

de.name: Kruzifixus
description: Das im Todesjahr des vor allen für seine Arbeiten in Kloster Stams bekannten Tiroler Bildhauers Andreas Thamasch geschaffene Kreuz gehört dem Typus des „Wund“- oder „Blutheilands“ an und wird auch als „Pestkreuz bezeichnet“. Mit seinem letzten Werk hat Thamasch ein besonders ausdrucksvolles Beispiel dieser Art geschaffen, das ergreifende Antlitz von Pein gezeichnet, der Körper von Wunden übersät.

en.name: Crucifix
description: The cross, created by the sculptor of Stams Monastery, Andreas Thamasch in the year of his death, is a “wound” or “Blutheilands” crucifix and is also referred to as a “Plague Cross”. With his last work Thamasch succeeded in creating an especially expressive example of this type; the stirring face wracked with torment, the body covered with wounds.

ar.name: سجادة أردبيل
description: هذه السجادة الرائعة صنعت كواحدة من زوج متطابق وإن نظيرتها محفوظة في متحف فكتوريا وألبرت في لندن . ووفقا لتوقيعهما المتطابقين فإن السجادتين كانتا من عمل مقصود كاشان وربما هو الذي قام بتحضير التصاميم وأشرف على المشروع. وقد كانتا سجادتين ملكيتين وربما أمر بصنعهما شاه طهماسب (حكم خلال 1524 – 76) حيث من الممكن أنهما كانتا من أجل ضريح جده في أردبيل. ويوجد نقش تماما أعلى التوقيع المؤرخ لكل سجادة وهو مقطع شعري فارسي مكتوب من قبل الشارع الفارسي الشهير في القرن الرابع عشر حافظ:"" ليس لدي  ملجأ في هذا العالم سوى العتبة / رأسي لا يوجد له مكان يستريح فيه غير هذه البوابة.""

en.name: Ardabil Carpet
description: This spectacular carpet was made as one of a matched pair, and its mate survives in the Victoria and Albert Museum, London. According to their identical signatures, the carpets were the work of Maqsud of Kashan, probably the one who prepared the designs and oversaw the project. They were royal carpets, perhaps commissioned for Shah Tahmasp (r. 1524–76), presumably for his ancestral shrine at Ardabil. Inscribed just above the dated signature of each carpet is a Persian couplet by the renowned fourteenth-century poet Hafiz: "I have no refuge in this world other than thy threshold / My head has no resting place other than this doorway."
holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)

de.name: Langhausfresko
description: Das große Deckenbild über dem Gemeinderaum steht ganz in der Thematik der Verherrlichung des Glaubens und der Kirche. In der Mitte ein Triumphwagen mit Christus und der Ecclesia im päpstlichen Ornat, gezogen von den vier Evangelistensymbolen bzw. apokalyptischen Wesen, die von Johannes dem Täufer geführt werden. Dazu Symbole der Erlösung (Kreuz, Lamm), des Endes der Zeiten (Chronos) und des Weltgerichts (Gerichtsengel, Buße), die auf die Erfüllung der Heilsgeschichte verweisen. In hell strahlender Farbigkeit schafft Zeiller hier eine Figurenkomposition von großer Plastizität und Eindringlichkeit, die die barocke Bildrhetorik mit Leben erfüllt.

en.name: Nave fresco
description: The large ceiling picture is entirely devoted to the glorification of faith and the church. In the centre a triumphal chariot with Christ and the ecclesia in papal regalia, pulled by the four evangelist symbols, i.e. apocalyptical beasts led by John the Baptist. In addition, symbols of redemption (the cross and the lamb), the end of time (Chronos) and the Last Judgement (the angel of judgement, penitence) which allude to the fulfilment of God’s plan of salvation. Using luminous colours, Zeiller succeeded in creating a figurative composition of great plasticity and forcefulness which fills the Baroque pictorial rhetoric with life.

en.name: *Arab Vase*
names: *Jarrón Árabe recientemente adquirido por el Museo*
description: Drawing of a vase known as "The Alhambra vase". The ceramic vase is a good example of the development of the Nasrid workshops. This vase came from the church of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción in Hornos (Jaén) and it was acquired by the National Museum of Archaeology in 1875. This type of vase is very rare and few of them have survived.

en.name: Coupled-column Prayer Rug
description: A prayer rug where the creamy-white field is decorated with a triple arch on double columns in yellow, red, blue, and green. Between each pair of columns is a row of lozenges in yellow and red. The spandrel is decorated with a diaper of geometrical scrolls in white, reserving in the ground double arrow motifs in yellow and red. Across the top of the field is a panel with stalks of lilies alternating with other plants (probably tulips) in yellow, red, light and dark blue, and green on a creamy-yellow ground. The arches or so-called *vandykes* along the bottom of the panel are in blue and yellow and enclose arabesques in white, red, blue, and green. In the border is a row of compartments in blue, yellow, or green with floral devices in yellow, red, blue, and green. The guard bands contain a repeat pattern of a flower and leaf motif in white and red on a yellow ground (inner guard band) or in yellow (or green) and red on a white ground (outer guard band).
dates: Hegira Early 12th to early 13th century / AD 18th century
place: Kula district, probably western Anatolia, Turkey, Asia

de.name: Stadtpfarrkirche Gmunden
names: Pfarrkirche Jungfrau Maria / Pfarrkirche Erscheinung des Herrn oder Dreikönigskirche
description:
In der Innenstadt steht die aus dem Mittelalter stammende (Pfarr)Kirche auf einer Anhöhe und dominiert von dort seit jeher das Stadtbild von Gmunden. Im 15./16. Jahrhundert hat man sie mit einem Friedhof umgeben. Im 17. und 18. Jahrhundert begann man die Kirche – in Form von Anbauten, Neuausstattungen und Dekorationen – zu barockisieren. Die berühmten Statuen auf den Hochaltar kamen im 17. Jahrhundert dazu, der wenig später erneuert wurde, und man erwarb weitere Kunstwerke und den Taufstein. Eine umfassende Barockisierung fand im 18. Jahrhundert statt. Damals wurden der Turm und die Eingangshalle hinzugefügt und der Innenraum dem Stil der Zeit gemäß ausgestattet.  
Als seltenes Beispiel eines Gotteshauses ist die Kirche nicht EINER heiligen Person oder EINEM historischen religiösen Ereignis gewidmet, sondern zweien: sie wurde im Mittelalter der Jungfrau Maria geweiht und später auch noch der Epiphanie (im 17. Jahrhundert). Das geschah vermutlich in der Zeit, als man für den Hochaltar die prachtvolle Statuengruppe der Anbetung der Könige anfertigen ließ.

Die Pfarrkirche wurde, was typisch in Österreich ist, im Mittelalter erbaut und während des Barock erweitert und dekorativ überarbeitet. Dieselbe architektonische Entwicklung durchlief die aufstrebende landesfürstliche Stadt Gmunden, die zunächst aus mächtigen mittelalterlichen Bauten bestand. Im 17. und 18. Jahrhundert fügte man etliche neue Gebäude hinzu oder barockisierte ältere Bauwerke.  
Im 17. Jahrhundert beauftragte man im Zug der Barockisierung der Kirche einen der bekanntesten Bildhauer der Zeit, Statuen für den Hochaltar zu gestalten. Ungefähr vierzig Jahre später fügte ein renommierter Architekt den Turm mit Zwiebelhelm und Laterne hinzu, der wie viele barocke Kirchtürme in Österreich das Wahrzeichen der Stadt wurde.

(1654-1698)
history:
Parallel zur wirtschaftlichen Entwicklung der Region entfaltete sich die Stadt Gmunden seit dem Mittelalter. Es gab eigentlich nur ein Hindernis zu überwinden: man musste die Stadt verkehrstechnisch öffnen. Sie liegt am Nordende des langen und schmalen Traunsees, der von teils steilen Bergen umgeben ist, weswegen es über die Jahrhunderte keine Verbindung zu Land gab. Transporte erfolgten ausschließlich über den See. Unbeeinflusst davon lebten Stadt und Bürger im Wohlstand, da es schon lange den außerordentlich gewinnbringenden (Salz)Abbau gab.  
Als die goldene Ära des Salzhandels endete, nahmen die Bürger einen Richtungswechsel vor – mit dem Entdecken des Salzes als Heilmittel bauten sie einen neuen wirtschaftlichen Zweig auf. Gmunden wurde ein bekanntes Sole-Heilbad und in Folge eine beliebte Sommerfrische der wohlhabenden und aristokratischen Gesellschaft Wiens.

en.name: Gmunden Parish Church
names: Parish Church of the Virgin or Parish Church of the Assumption of the Virgin / Parish Church of the Epiphany
description:
Right in the city, the medieval (parish) church is situated on an elevation and since then has dominated Gmunden’s skyline. In the 15th/16th century it became surrounded by a graveyard, in the 17th and 18th century baroquisation in the form of additions, fittings and decoration took place. The high altar got in the 17th century its famous statues and other artworks, such as the baptismal font. An extensive baroquisation took place in the 18th century. The tower and the entrance hall were added and the interior was overworked in the style of the epoch.  
As a rare example of a place of worship, the church was not only dedicated to *one* holy person or *one* historic religious event, but to two: it was in the Middle Ages consecrated to the Holy Virgin and later to the Epiphany (in the 17th century). This probably happened when the high altar got the magnificent group of statues, the Adoration of the Magi.

Typically Austrian, the Gmunden parish church was built in the Middle Ages and extended and decoratively overworked in the Baroque era. The up-and-coming princely city of Gmunden went through the same architectural development: initially there were mighty buildings from the Middle Ages, in the 17th and 18th century new edifices were added or old buildings were baroquized.  
In the course of baroquization, one of the most popular sculptors was commissioned in the 17th century to create statues for the high altar. About forty years later a well-known architect added the tower with onion-shaped roof and lantern. Like many baroque church towers in Austria, this became the landmark of the town.
dates:
1270: first documentary mention  
First half of the 14th century: construction of church  
Second half of the 17th century: start of baroquisation (exterior and interior)  
First third of the 17th century: Holy Virgin statue  
17th century: baptismal font  
1678: Epiphany statues  
1679: high altar (modified about 1860)  
1685: Anna altar  
About 1690: St Elizabeth and St Zachariah statues  
End 17th century: St Barbara and St Margaretha statues  
1713–18: construction of tower  
1723: entrance hall  
First half of 18th century: St Peter and St Paul statues
artist: Architecture: Gothic basilica 14th century: unknown; tower: Johann Michael Prunner (1669–1739); statues at high altar: Thomas Schwanthaler (1634–1707); Anna altar, statues at Anna altar, altarpiece(?), statues of St Elizabeth and St Zachariah at high altar: Michael Zürn the younger (1654–98)
history:
Simultaneously with the region’s economic development, the city of Gmunden was growing and developing since the Middle Ages. There was only one obstacle to overcome: one had to open it for the road traffic. The town is situated on the North end of the long and narrow Traunsee which is surrounded by partially steep mountains, and it was because of this over the centuries without a land route. Transport took place by ship through the lake. Unaffected by this, city and citizens lived in prosperity as there had always been profitable (salt) mining.  
When the golden era of salt trade ended, the citizens changed direction – the salt’s healing power was discovered and a new branch of industry was born. Gmunden became popular as a brine spa and consequently as a summer retreat for the noble and wealthy from Vienna.

en.name: Apses in the Mother Church
description: The Mother Church (Chiesa Madre) is located in the Quarter called Ruccera, which, together with the Rabato Quarter, formed the fundamental nucleus of the Arab-Norman walled city, known later as Terra Vecchia. Only the three apses with semi-cylindrical volume remain of the original Norman church, and in later eras windows were opened up in addition to the one in the central apse originating from the Norman period. According to a reconstruction of 1900, the Mother Church, dedicated to Santa Maria Maddalena, was subdivided into three naves by a series of bells sustained by arches on pillars rather than on columns. This characteristic which would seem to testify to the construction belonging to the 12th century, a time of the County, and in particular attributing the foundation to the Countess Giuditta, daughter of Great Count Ruggero. In 1656, threatened with ruin, the church was completely rebuilt by the architect Michele Blasco, with the exception of the apses, which from the inside, were remodelled with decorative displays of the baroque period.

es.name: Ábsides de la Iglesia Matriz
description: La Iglesia Matriz está ubicada en el barrio de Ruccera, que constituía, junto con el de Rabato, el núcleo fundamental de la ciudad amurallada arábigo-normanda, denominada posteriormente Terra Vecchia. De la iglesia original normanda quedan solamente los tres ábsides de volumen semicilíndrico, en los cuales se abrieron en épocas sucesivas más ventanas, aparte de la del ábside central del periodo normando. Según una reconstrucción de 1900, la Iglesia Matriz, dedicada a Santa María Magdalena, estaba dividida en tres naves por una sucesión de crujías sostenidas por arcos sobre pilares en vez de columnas, característica que parece atestiguar la pertenencia de la construcción al siglo XII, periodo del Condado, y en particular se atribuye su fundación a la condesa Giuditta, hija del gran conde Ruggero. En 1656, el arquitecto Michele Blasco reconstruyó toda la iglesia, que amenazaba ruina, a excepción de los ábsides, que en el interior fueron remodelados con decoración de la época barroca.

de.name: Planung aus der Gründungsurkunde: Hl. Grab mit Schlupfwallfahrt
description: Die in der Gründungsurkunde überlieferte Planung von Johann Jakob Herkomer sah als Besonderheit ein heiliges Grab in der Unterkirche vor, eine sogenannte “Schlupfwallfahrt“, wie Herkomer sie auch in seiner eigenen Hauskapelle in Sameister gebaut hatte. Der Zugang sollte durch einen niedrigen Durchlass erfolgen. Obgleich Herkomers Ideen in die Urkunde eingegangen sind, wurden sie nicht umgesetzt, vielleicht aus Kostengründen, und durch die einfachere Neuplanung Hafeneggers ersetzt.

en.name: Plans from the founding charter: Holy sepulchre with “Schlupfwallfahrt”
description: The plans from Johann Jakob Herkomer contained in the founding charter envisaged a special feature, a holy sepulchre in the crypt, a so-called “Schlupfwallfahrt”, as built by Herkomer in his own private chapel in Sameister. Access was to be provided by a low passage. Although Herkomer’s ideas found their way into the founding charter they were not realised, possibly on cost grounds, and were replaced by the simpler revised plans from Hafenegger.

en.name: Mercenary’s helmet
description: It began when a farmer in the canton of Ticino found an old gravestone in 1900. Soon it became clear that what lay buried there was not just a collection of old bones. In fact, there were over 500 such graves, all dating from the Iron Age. About one-fifth of the burials were warriors who had been interred with their lances, shields, swords, and helmets.The Roman Empire had taken to hiring mercenaries to aid its expansion to the north towards the end of the Iron Age. Mercenaries used their own weapons and armour, and the helmet found in the grave has been identified as belonging to a mercenary who came from the Central Alps. The mercenaries would return to their homes after completing their period of service. When they died, they were given a warrior’s funeral as befitted their status, like this man from Giubiasco, whose origins are revealed by the shape of his helmet. It’s all in the shape. Even in archaeology.
keywords: Helmet; Mercenary; Iron Age; Bronze; Excavation; Ticino

ar.name: القبة الصغيرة.
description:
البناء مكعب الشكل، في الحديقة النورمندية الكبيرة، سقفة على شكل نصف كرة مثبتة بأقواس متطاولة، تقوم على أعمدة في جهاته الأربع، كان يستخدم للاستراحة أثناء الصيد اتقاء من حرارة الشمس الشديدة خلا ل النهار.  
وبني على مثال "القبة" وتزيزا "عزيزة"، وتم تشييد هذه الابنية في النصف الثاني من القرن الثاني عشر خلال فترة حكم غولييمو الثاني.

جناحٌ منفتحٌ على جوانبه الأربع بعقود مدببة، ومغطى بقبة نصف كروية، شُيد خلال النصف الثاني من القرن 13، تحت حكم جيوم الثاني. من المحتمل، أن هذا الجناح كان ينتمي لتصميم ماء القبة، ويمكن التفكير بأنه كان بمثابة موضع للتوقف والاستجمام خلال فصل الصيف، أيام مباريات الصيد التي كانت تجري داخل الحديقة النورمندية الكبيرة.

en.name: Piccola Cuba (Little Cuba).
description: This cubic pavilion is open on all four sides through pointed arches and covered with a domed roof. It was probably part of the Cuba’s fishpond and was most likely used as a place to rest and shelter from the heat of summer during the hunting parties that were held in the large Norman park. Among other pavilions, this park also contained the Cuba and Zisa palaces.

es.name: Pequeña Cuba
description:
Se trata de un pabellón de forma cúbica, abierto en sus cuatro lados por arcos ojivales y cubierto por una cúpula. Con toda probabilidad se encontraba en el estanque de la Cuba y servía como lugar de descanso y refugio del calor veraniego durante las batidas de caza que tenían como escenario el gran parque normando. Entre otros edificios, este parque también albergaba los palacios de la Cuba y la Zisa.  
Se erigió en la segunda mitad del siglo XII, durante el reinado de Guglielmo II.

Probablemente se encontraba en el estanque de la Cuba, y era lugar de descanso y de alivio del calor estival durante las batidas de caza en el gran parque normando.

Le pavillon, de forme cubique, est ouvert sur les quatre côtés par des arcades ogivales et coiffé d'une coupole hémisphérique.
