en.name: Monastery of San Michele in Bosco, Library
description:
The library is composed of three rooms in a row, lluminated by side windows. The central room is large and square, with three domed vaults separated by arches. The other rooms, the vestibule and the room dedicated to mathematical and scientific instruments, have vaulted ceilings.  
All the rooms are completely decorated with illusive architectural features which frame the figures. This homogenous decoration endows the small space with a magnificent and new face.  
The subject painted by Domenico Maria Canuti is that of Wisdom, a combination of science and religion. The complex meaning of the theological allegories is explained in a booklet specially published in 1681, to explain their significance after the work was finished.  
The ceiling of the main room, while separated by arches, shows the same decorative theme. Wisdom is celebrated: in the centre Divine Wisdom dominates Human Wisdom, at the sides allegorical figures warn against a daring use of knowledge and demonstrate how study and research must have Good as their main aim. The decoration is completed by painted telamones supporting the vaults on their shoulders, the Allegories of the Four Continents and of the main Doctrines in the lunettes.  
In the Vestibule of the library, the “sfondato” shows the Four Human Temperaments symbolically linked with the allegories of the Four Elements painted in the pendentives.  
In the last room are depicted the Cardinal Virtues in the pendentives and the Four Fathers of the Church as monochromes on the walls; in the middle of the ceiling the archangel Michael pleads with God to help the sciences and virtues.  
The Paintings in the three rooms are connected by the painted architecture by Enrico Haffner. The style emphasizes the figures without oppressing them and creates a homogeneous texture rich of inventions.

The church and monastery of San Michele in Bosco were built on a hill above Bologna in place of a former church dedicated to St. Michael dating to the 12th century. The first shrine on this site dates back to the 4th century. The Olivetan Fathers, living here since 1364, rebuilt the church and the monastery between 1437 and 1447; the buildings were refurbished again in 1517-23. The works were finished by 1660: the baroque library, painted by Domenico Maria Canuti and Enrico Haffner, is a significant example of Baroque painted decoration. The octagonal cloister painted by the Carracci and the refectory decorated by Vasari and his pupils are also some of the highlights of the architectural complex. Since 1896 the former monastery has housed the Istituto Ortopedico Rizzoli, a hospital.
artist: Giovan Giacomo Monti; Domenico Maria Canuti; Enrico Haffner
history: The Library was commissioned by abbot Taddeus Pepoli, an intellectual and patron of the arts. In 1627 he entrusted the architect Giovan Giacomo Monti with rebuilding the former 16th century library, in order to create a grander and newer edifice. The architect amplified the space with new vaulted ceilings seven feet high. In 1677 the rooms were covered with frescoes by Domenico Maria Canuti. He was assisted by Enrico Haffner, a painter specialized in illusionistic painting (quadrature). The decorations follow a complex and intellectual iconographic program which was most likely created by Pepoli who patronized the work. The library was inaugurated in 1681. After the suppression of the Olivetan order the monastery was first converted into a prison and later became the summer residence of the Papal representative. The library was stripped of its furniture, bookcases and instruments and used for rehearsals. In 1922, when the monastery was being used as a hospital, the library was restored. Today it holds a precious collection of books concerning orthopaedics.
keywords: Figural decoration; quadratura; allegory
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Biblioteca del convento di San Michele in Bosco
description:
La biblioteca è composta da tre sale poste in asse e illuminate da aperture laterali: la sala centrale, vera e propria biblioteca, è rettangolare, ha maggiori dimensioni e presenta un soffitto con tre volte a catino divise da arconi trasversali; anche le altre due stanze, il vestibolo d'ingresso e un vano destinato ad accogliere strumenti matematici e scientifici, sono voltate.  
Tutti gli spazi sono interamente affrescati con quadrature architettoniche dipinte che fanno da cornice alle scene figurative. Oltre ai soffitti sono ornate con affreschi anche le pareti, le lunette e i pennacchi: questa uniformità decorativa conferisce agli spazi, di dimensioni relativamente modeste, un aspetto grandioso e innovativo.   
Il tema iconografico del ciclo pittorico svolto da Domenico Maria Canuti è quello della Sapienza, argomento affrontato come un incontro tra scienza e religione. Il significato complesso delle allegorie teologiche, rese necessario la realizzazione di un opuscolo di spiegazioni, divulgato nel 1681 al termine dei lavori.  
Le volte della sala principale, sebbene separate da archi, presentano una concezione decorativa unitaria. Qui il tema della Sapienza raggiunge il suo apice: al centro è la Sapienza divina che emerge su quella umana mentre nelle volte laterali le allegorie ammoniscono circa un uso troppo audace del sapere e illustrano come lo studio e la ricerca debbano sempre essere diretti al Bene. Completano la decorazione di questa sala i termini dipinti nei pennacchi che paiono sostenere la copertura, le allegorie dei Continenti e delle Discipline con i più illustri rappresentanti raffigurati nelle lunette.  
Nella stanza di accesso alla libreria, lo sfondato mostra raffigurati i quattro *Temperamenti* dell'uomo collegati simbolicamente alle allegorie dei quattro *Elementi* realizzate nei pennacchi.  
Nell'ultima sala sono raffigurate le *Virtù Cardinali* nei pennacchi e i quattro *Padri della Chiesa* dipinti a monocromo sulle pareti; lo sfondato della volta mostra l'arcangelo Michele che supplica le divinità di assistere le scienze e le virtù.  
Le pitture delle tre sale sono unite dall'architettura dipinta realizzata da Enrico Haffner che valorizza le figure senza sovrastarle e crea un tessuto decorativo omogeneo e ricco di invenzioni.

La chiesa e il convento di San Michele in Bosco sorgono sulla collina bolognese nel sito dove esisteva una chiesa intitolata a San Michele, nota dal XII secolo, eretta probabilmente su preesistenze del IV secolo. I monaci olivetani, presenti sul luogo dal 1364, riedificarono la chiesa e costruirono il convento tra il 1437 ed il 1447, trasformati poi nel 1517–23. La vicenda costruttiva si concluse intorno al 1660: seicentesca è la biblioteca, notevole esempio di decorazione pittorica barocca realizzata da Domenico Maria Canuti e Enrico Haffner. All'interno da ricordare anche il chiostro ottagonale con pitture della scuola dei Carracci e il refettorio affrescato da allievi di Giorgio Vasari. Dal 1896 il complesso conventuale è sede dell'Istituto Ortopedico Rizzoli.
artist: Gian Giacomo Monti; Domenico Maria Canuti; Enrico Haffner
history: L'attuale biblioteca fu realizzata per volontà dell'abate del convento Taddeo Pepoli, erudito e mecenate, che nel 1627 incaricò l'architetto Giovan Giacomo Monti di trasformare la preesistente libreria cinquecentesca, ritenuta inadeguata alle esigenze e al gusto fastoso dell'epoca. L'architetto trasformò lo spazio sopraelevandolo di sette piedi e dotandolo di soffitti voltati. Successivamente, nel 1677, le sale furono integralmente affrescate da Domenico Maria Canuti in collaborazione con il pittore quadraturista Enrico Haffner, i quali raffigurarono un complesso e colto programma iconografico ideato probabilmente dal priore Pepoli, committente dell'opera e inaugurato nel 1681. In seguito alla soppressione dell'ordine Olivetano e alla chiusura del convento, adibito prima a carcere e poi a residenza del legato pontificio, la biblioteca venne spogliata dei suoi arredi, scaffalature e strumenti, e utilizzata come sala per i ricevimenti. Nel 1922, già divenuto il convento sede dell'Istituto Rizzoli, la biblioteca restaurata tornò ad accogliere il patrimonio librario consistente in una delle più complete e rare collezioni esistenti in campo ortopedico.
keywords: Decorazione figurale; quadratura; allegoria, illusiuonismo pittura murale, biblioteca

en.name: Great Mosque of Nur al-Din
description:
Known by the residents of Homs as the Great Mosque it is one of the most important historical monuments of the city, second only to the mosque of Khalid ibn al-Walid, as well as being the largest. The site, used for spiritual purposes even before Christian times, was probably a temple to the Sun God, Apollo. Parts of the mosque, it is thought, were formerly a church dedicated to Saint John the Baptist. Corinthian column capitals in the mosque courtyard and in the decorated lintels represent most of these remains. In 359/969, during the Arab conquests, the Byzantine Emperor Nisifor Fokas destroyed the mosque that was on this site. Thus, when Nur al-Din took control of Syria during the 6th/12th century, he strengthened the Arab frontier against the Byzantines and he gave each major city a new mosque, including this one in Homs. On the south wall of the mosque is an inscription commemorating the Mamluk Sultan al-Zahir Baybars’ restoration of the mosque in the 7th/13th century.  
The mosque is rectangular, approximately 5.323 m-sq, divided into a prayer-hall and courtyard of nearly equal size. This layout is similar to many of the Umayyad mosque layouts as found in Syria, such as the Great Umayyad Mosque in Damascus (I.1.f) and the Jami’ al-‘Umari in Bosra (II.1.c). The entrance to the mosque is on the south side and may have been part of a different building that pre-dates the mosque. It leads directly to the prayerhall. There is a western gate, which also leads directly to the prayer-hall; this latter one is modern, built in the 1950s. The final and main gate, renovated in 1197/1783, leads to the courtyard of the mosque.  
The prayer-hall is an elongated rectangle measuring 17 m x 100 m. The ceiling’s construction comprises a cross-vaulted stone resting on 14 stone, square pillars and a small dome. Only some parts of the prayer-hall date to the Ayybuid period: the room next to the *mihrab* and the marble dado rail and marble *minbar*, the main *mihrab* in the southern wall, as well as two smaller flanking *mirhabs*. On the top of the main *mihrab*, there are important traces of a mosaic panel. Scholars continue to debate whether it is Umayyad or Ayyubid. As for the mosque courtyard, it is also rectangular and open to the sky, surrounded by an arcade on each side. Now removed, a water basin with a well covered by a small dome furnished the courtyard. There are also the remains of an Ayyubid *madrasa*. In the middle of the northern arcade there is a circular tower, opposite to which are two circular plaques of white stone resting on pillars, these were sundials. A shorter pillar made of granite, 98 cm high, is situated between the two circular plaques and would have been used to determine the angle of the sun, especially useful for determining the time of the Asr prayer (between noon and sunset). As for the minaret, located in the south-western part of the mosque and made of basalt stone, it follows the Umayyad style of a square-based minaret.  
The Nuri Mosque is contemporaneous to the Church of Saint Elian and, in addition to its architectural and artistic importance, its patron, Nur al-Din, was a leader renowned for his religious tolerance to the different communities of Syria.

ar.name: قارورة ماء
description: صُنعت قارورة الماء الملونة هذه في إزنيق أوسوراهي، وزُينت بزخارف مذهلة بأشكال الزهور والأرابيسك. وقد تم نقش الزخارف على سطح الزجاجة بأداة حادة قبل وضع الألوان، مما أعطى الفنان قالباً للعمل، وسمح له بإضافة تفاصيل إضافية حسب رغبته. إن الحجم الكبير غير المعتاد لهذه الزجاجة، والجودة العالية لزخارفها، يجعلانها مثالاً رائعاً لهذا النوع من القوارير.

en.name: Water bottle
description: This polychrome Iznik water bottle, *orsürahi*, is decorated with striking, stylised vegetal and arabesque motifs. The decoration was sketched out into the surface of the slip with a sharp instrument before the colours were applied, giving the artist a template from which to work but also allowing him to add additional painted details as he wished. The unusually large size of this bottle, and the spirited quality of its decoration, make it a particularly fine example of its genre.
keywords: Iznik; Ceramics; Floral; Turkey

en.name: Jewellery for horses – Type 2
short_description: These strings of jewels were used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. The chain consists of a variety of differently shaped beads which would bounce against each other to create a tinkling noise and announce the arrival of the rider.
keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewels

en.name: *The Great Hall of the Musée Assyrien in the Louvre*
names: Taken from the collection *Topographie de Paris*, "1er arrondissement, 1er quartier, Le Louvre"
short_description: In May 1847, the world's first " Musée Assyrien" was opened at the Louvre. This was enabled by the arrival of 37 enormous bas-reliefs discovered by Paul-Émile Botta (1802–1870), the French consul in Mosul, at the site of Khorsabad. Botta, a diplomat, doctor, explorer and archaeologist, organised excavations in the hope of rediscovering Nineveh and its Assyrian monuments, and thus brought about the discovery of Khorsabad which in turn aided and accelerated the deciphering of Cuneiform in Mesopotamia. The "Musée Assyrien" pictured here was a great success and  attracted much attention on its opening in Paris in 1847.
keywords: Assyrian antiquities; Musée du Louvre

fr.name: *La grande salle du musée assyrien au Louvre*
names: Extrait du Recueil. Topographie de Paris. Ier arrondissement. 1er quartier. Le Louvre
short_description: En mai 1847 est inauguré au Louvre le premier « Musée assyrien » du monde. Cette création a été rendue possible par l’arrivée de 37 bas-reliefs monumentaux découverts sur le site de Khorsabad par Paul-Emile Botta (1802–1870), consul de France à Mossoul. Botta, tour à tour diplomate, médecin, explorateur, archéologue, espérait en effet redécouvrir Ninive et les monuments assyriens et organisa des fouilles qui entraînèrent la découverte de Khorsabad, ce qui permit entre autres d’accélérer le déchiffrement du cunéiforme de Mésopotamie. Le « Musée assyrien », visible sur l’image, eut un grand succès de curiosité à Paris en 1847.
keywords: antiquités assyriennes; Musée du Louvre

en.name: *One Thousand and One Nights*: decorative sketch of the palace gardens. Façade of an
short_description: The collection *One Thousand and One Nights* was translated into French in the early 18th century. The rise of Orientalism caused it to become extremely popular, appearing as the subject of numerous editions, adaptations, etc. In the 19th century, a tale from the collection was staged in one of Paris' most famous theatres (the Théâtre du Châtelet), and, as this image shows, the theatre was redecorated as an "Oriental palace" for the occasion.
keywords: Orientalism; one thousand and one nights

fr.name: Les mille et une nuits: esquisse de décor: les Jardins du palais. Façade d'un palais oriental
short_description: Le recueil des *Mille et une nuits* est traduit en français au début du XVIIIe siècle. Avec l’orientalisme, il devient incontournable et fait l’objet de nombreuses éditions, adaptations, etc. Ici, une féérie tirée des *Mille et une nuits*, portée sur la scène d’un des plus célèbres théâtres parisiens du XIXe siècle (le théâtre du Châtelet), entraîne la construction d’un décor de « palais oriental ».
keywords: Orientalisme; Milel et une nuits

en.name: Cruz de Portugal
description: The *Cruz de Portugal* (the Portuguese Cross) is one of the loveliest Manueline crosses to have been conserved. According to documentation, it was customary for the local people to have crosses made to mark holy ground. The arms of the Gothic cross in honey-toned limestone are carved with foliate rosettes, and set in a niche supported by a profusely decorated column. The *Crucifixion* is represented on one side and on the other side is a *Pietà* with the Virgin holding the body of her dead Son.

en.name: Al-Naoor Waterwheel
description:
A wooden waterwheel known locally as naoor (plural: nawa'ir), traditionally used to lift water for agricultural irrigation along the upper Euphrates, from Syria into Anbar governorate in western Iraq. The town of Hit (north-west of Baghdad) is at the south-eastern limit of the area of their use.  
  
The example pictured (around 5 metres in diameter) is a small replica constructed by a waterfront coffee shop owner around the year 2000, but most nawa'ir were larger, ranging from 8-12 metres in diameter. They were constructed from lengths of mulberry wood (known for its durabiliity), cut to size and connected with wooden pegs hammered into place. No metal was traditionally used in the waterwheel's construction: this modern example has corrugated metal paddles to power its rotation , but traditionally this function was served by similar rectangular paddles made of small straight sticks attached together in parallel.  
  
A traditional naoor had twenty-four wooden spokes and twenty-four ceramic jars attached to its outer circumference, tied on with palm fibre cordage. As the river current caused the wheels to rotate, the jars would raise water from the river and pour it into an aqueduct at the top of the stone platform, which fed into irrigation channels leading to nearby farms. Traditionally, several farms or families would share a waterwheel and distribute the water between them, each using it during agreed hours of the day; this whole community would also be involved in its construction and installation, which could take up to a month.  
  
According to local sources, this technology has been in use since Akkadian times to solve the problem that the river level in this region is much lower than the surrounding ground. The stone foundations (dahlia) supporting today's nawa'ir are estimated to be around 400 years old, and were built using a specific type of lime-based mortar that hardens underwater.  
  
Many traditional nawa'ir were destroyed in 1967 by a devastating flood on the Euphrates. Although some were rebuilt, electric pumps began to take over their function in the 1970s. The nawa'ir remained an important feature of local memory and were celebrated in reconstructions such as the one pictured. Between 2019-2021, a campaign by local residents led to the rehabilitation of four large waterwheels in Hit, and to their inscription on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2021. Similar revivals have taken place in other parts of Anbar, notably in Haditha, where 24 waterwheels are said to be in operation.
holder: Open Museum Initiative for Water Culture
dates:
Naoor, wooden waterwheel: AH ca. 1400 / AD ca. 2000  
  
Dahlia, stone base: AH ca. 800 / AD ca. 1600
keywords: Water; naoor; waterwheel; wood; aqueduct; irrigation
materials: Wood (mulberry boughs); joined with wooden pegs. Base: stone, lime-based mortar; hardens underwater; Digital photography.
tags: joined with wooden pegs. Base: stone, lime-based mortar
partner: Open Museum Initiative for Water Cultures

en.name: Confronted animal rug
description: When this rug was discovered, its unusual design of confronted animals with smaller animals within was otherwise known only in a rug depicted in a Sienese painting of about 1410, *The Marriage of the Virgin*, in the collection of the National Gallery, London. The pattern of the rug in the painting, partially obscured by standing figures, was not comprehensible without this example. The purchase, hailed in carpet-collecting circles, brought one of the best preserved, earliest Turkish carpets in the world to the Museum. The field design probably derives from medieval textiles patterned with single or paired animals in compartments.
keywords: Ottoman; Turkey; Anatolia; wool; textile; animal carpet; animal decoration; domestic furnishings; figurative decoration; geometric decoration; European influence; Ottoman carpet
materials: Wool (warp, weft, and pile); symmetrically knotted pile

en.name: *Hagia Sophia. General view*
description: Photographic print that is part of an album of different Istanbul images taken by the studio of the three Armenian brothers who, in 1880, opened a headquarters in this city. It shows the central nave of the Mosque of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya Camii), under the main dome, facing the Eastern apse where the altar has been replaced by a *mihrab*. On the left, in the transept, the pavilion for the sultan's personal prayer. A group of men are sitting on the ground, on carpets that cover the entire surface, listening attentively. This kind of album had great success with 19th century European travellers.
keywords: Istanbul; souvenirs; memorabilia

en.name: *The Glory of St. Ignatius of Loyola*
description: The glory of the founder saint of the Jesuits dominates the middle of the vault of the chapel. It is inspired by the great decoration with the same subject painted by Andrea Pozzo in Rome.
place: Chapel of the Jesuit novitiate, vault
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: *La Gloria di S. Ignazio di Loyola*
description: La gloria del santo fondatore dei Gesuiti domina il centro della volta della cappella. E' ispirato alla grande decorazione con lo stesso soggetto dipinta da Andrea Pozzo a Roma
place: Cappella del noviziato dei Gesuiti, volta

de.name: Hochaltar
description: Der Hochaltar, ausgeführt vom Tischlermeister Johann Jaufer aus Innsbruck, birgt eine spätgotische Marienstatue. Das barocke Altarwerk bildet den Rahmen zur Inszenierung des älteren Kultbildes und wird damit zum Mittelpunkt der gesamten Bildausstattung der Kirche und des ikonographischen Programms. Das hochziehbare Altarbild mit der Darstellung der Himmelfahrt Mariens stammt von Mölck. Es findet seine Fortsetzung in Deckenfresken mit einem Marienzyklus.

en.name: High altar
description: The high altar, the work of master carpenter Johann Laufer from Innsbruck, incorporates a Late Gothic statue of the Virgin Mary. The Baroque altar constitutes the frame for the staging of the older devotional image and thus forms the centrepiece of the church’s entire pictorial inventory. The raiseable altarpiece depicting the Assumption of Mary originates from Mölck. It finds its continuation in the ceiling frescoes depicting the Mariological cycle.
artist: Johann Adam Ritter von Mölck (1718–1794); Johann Jaufer [n.d.]

en.name: *The Qadous path*
short_description: The clever use of light in this painting helps illustrate the beauty of the countryside around Algiers in the 19th century. It highlights the richness of the vegetation in the area surrounding the Algerian notability's country homes.

fr.name: *Le chemin du qadous*
short_description: Ce tableau aux magnifiques jeux de lumière, est une très belle illustration de la campagne qui environnait Alger au XIXème siècle. Il témoigne en effet de la riche végétation qui abritait les maisons de campagne de la notabilité algéroise.

cs.name: Panna Marie jako královna nebes
description: V letech 1736–1745 byl interiér kostela nově vybaven. Plochy všech kleneb pokrývá malba. V kněžišti Korunování P. Marie (královna andělů), v lodích Oslavy Krista, Ducha sv., P. Marie ad. Autor maleb byl kolem r. 1720 v Mnichově žákem předního jihoněmeckého freskaře C. D. Assama. Prostřednictvím Řádu německých rytířů přišel do Slezska a odtud na Moravu, r. 1743 se stal dvorním malířem hraběte Filipa Ludvíka ze Sinzendorfu.

en.name: The Virgin Mary as Queen of Heaven
description: In 1736–1745 the church was redecorated. The vaults are covered with fresco paintings. The Coronation of the Virgin Mary (Queen of Heaven) is in the chancel while in the naves are the Celebrations of Christ, the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary along with other works. The artist was a pupil of C. D. Assam, a leading south-German fresco painter who was active in Munich in around 1720. He came to Silesia and Moravia through the Order of German Knights and in 1743 he became court painter to Count Filip Ludvík of Sinzendorf.
place: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary

en.name: Mercedes-Benz 770 *Grosser*
description:
When Mercedes-Benz introduced the new 700 (codenamed the W07) in 1930, it had one thing in mind – to be the vehicle of choice for sovereigns and heads of states. Being the largest and most expensive Mercedes-Benz, only 117 units were produced from 1930 to 1938 in their Untertürkheim factory. The armoured Pullmann limousine accounted for 42 of these units. Emperor Hiroito of Japan acquired three of them, and two came to Portugal in 1938. Once there, one of the 770s famously belonged to Portuguese head of state Prof. António de Oliveira Salazar, having been one of several armoured models acquired for him. The history of armoured vehicles acquired in the name of Oliveira Salazar, then President of the Council of Ministers, forms one of the most curious chapters in Portugal’s history.  
  
After the failed bombing attempt on Sunday, 4 July 1937 on Avenida Barbosa du Bocage, when Salazar was on his way to morning Mass, the State Surveillance and Defense Police (PVDE) ordered two Type 770 Pullmansteel in October of that year. The order was made through the Mercedes-Benz agent in Lisbon, Sociedade Comercial Mattos Tavares, Lda, but given the specificity of the model, they transferred the order to the brand’s offices in Germany.  
  
According to the factory files, both chassis were completed on 18 January 1938 and the Pullmansteel bodies on 9 March. Both cars were then shipped to Lisbon on 12 April. They were registered in June 1938, in the name of PVDE, and were immediately made available to the Presidents of the Republic and the Council, General Óscar Carmona (AL-10-71, chassis # 182 067) and Prof. Oliveira Salazar (DA-10-72, chassis # 182 066).  
  
Salazar, who had not been consulted on the purchase of the cars, soon expressed his discontent, refusing to use the Mercedes-Benz assigned to him. This was not only because it was an ostentatious car, but also because it was thought to have been a gift from Hitler to the President of the Council. The car was used only once – on the occasion of the official visit of Generalissimo Franco in 1949. The car’s scant usage was by driver Raúl to transport visitors to and from Palacete de São Bento. Because of this, the odometer read only 6,000 kilometres when, seventeen years later, it was sold at a public auction by the Directorate-General for Finance.  
  
The auction was won after six counts by the scrap dealer Alfredo Nunes, who registered it in his name on 9 February 1955. It was sold shortly afterward to the Beato and Olivais Voluntary Firefighters to be used as their ambulance. The conversion costs however proved much too high, and they sold it on 16 June 1956 to João de Lacerda, to be displayed in the Museu do Caramulo.  
  
Nowadays, the car, having circulated since 1956, has clocked up 12,949 kilometres, most of which have been in Caramulo – to and from the maintenance garage. There was never a need to restore the car because from paintwork to chrome and upholstery, it is impeccable. Even the Buna rubber tires are original, being maintained at 40 pounds of pressure so as not to cause cracks in the flanks.  
  
The 770 in the Museu do Caramulo is considered by experts to be the best-kept and most perfect Mercedes-Benz Grosser in the world.

en.name: Historic Centre
description:
"The structure of Manueline Viana is easily seen today by studying the roads in the historic centre. They form an oblong, corresponding to the outline of the 14th-century walls that surrounded rectangular blocks of dwellings defined by a perpendicular grid, widening parallel to the river. The Porta de São Crispim opened at this side and the road crossed the town in a straight line in front of the New Parish Church to the Praça Velha and the Porta do Forno or the Porta de São Tiago, which led into Campo do Forno. Rua de São Pedro and Rua Grande ran in perpendicular lines to the other gates, Porta da Ribeira or Porta de São João, and Porta das Atafonas.  
The defending wall, built, essentially, between 1263 and 1374, has since disappeared, although its outline can still be traced. The names of some of the masters of works who worked there towards the end of this period are known, such as António Fernandes and João Domingues.  
Some of the Late Gothic houses in this area are of particular interest. The Casa dos Costa Barros, in Rua de São Pedro has splendid Manueline windows, that have something profoundly Baroque about them, on the main floor. In front of the Parish Church is the Casa dos Medalhões or the Casa dos Lunas, already Renaissance in style. The Casa de João Velho, at the side of the church, has a segmental arch on the ground floor and crossheaded windows that were quite common in the Late Gothic period. D. Manuel I stayed in this house in 1506 when he visited Viana.  
Some of the houses in this area have added historic interest; for example, the Casa de Pêro Galego in Viela da Parenta has a caravel carved in relief on the door lintel. In the Rua do Tourinho there is the Gothic Casa de Pedro Tourinho, the home of one of the first *donatários* or lord proprietors in Brazil, specifically of Porto Seguro.  
Just outside the walled perimeter there are other buildings, which either date back to or were heavily restored during the early 16th century. This is the case with the elegantly fronted Gothic Casa da Câmara, the Town Hall in the former Campo do Forno, now the Praça da República. Meetings used to be held under the triple arcade on the main floor. In view of the limited space available within the town’s walls, the market also began to be held here when the population increased dramatically in Manueline times.  
One of the best Manueline houses, although heavily restored later on, is the Casa da Carreira (in Rua Cândido dos Reis) built in 1527, by Fernão Brandão, who served in the forts at Safi and Azamor in North Africa. The façade retains some Late Manueline door and window frames."

en.name: Stefan Petrovic Knicanin (1809–1855)
short_description: Portrait of Stefan Petrovic Knicanin. The Serbian officer Stefan Petrovic Knicanin supported the Austrian Emperor during the 1848 revolution. In 1849 he returned to Serbia and fostered good relations between Serbia and Austria. He died in 1855 in Belgrade.
keywords: Stefan Petrovic Knicanin; Serbia

en.name: *Treaty of Peace and Trade between France and the Tunisian Regency*
short_description: The Treaty of Peace and Trade, signed between France and the Tunisian Regency, was written in both French and Arabic. It protected all French ships from attacks from Tunisian privateers, gave them access to every port in the country, and guaranteed all French nationals full security.
keywords: Hamuda Pacha Bey; capitulation treaty
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Traité capitulaire de paix et de commerce entre la France et la Régence de Tunis
short_description: Le traité capitulaire de paix et de commerce conclu entre la France et la Régence de Tunis fut rédigé dans les deux langues, arabe et français. Il mettait les navires français à l’abri des attaques des corsaires tunisiens et leur donnait accès à tous les ports du pays, garantissant à leurs nationaux une entière sécurité.
keywords: Hamouda Pacha Bey; Traité de capitulaton
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Great Mosque
description:
The Great Mosque of Kairouan is considered to be the oldest and most prestigious sanctuary in the Muslim West. Its architectural model served as an example for the majority of Ifriqiyan mosques until the arrival of the Ottomans. Through the diversity of its forms and the richness of its ornamental repertoire, it incarnates the essential elements fundamental to the school of Kairouanese architecture. The first oratory was built in 50/670 by ‘Uqba Ibn Nafi. Constructed using crumbly materials, it was completely rebuilt by Hassan Ibn Nu‘man in 84/703. The mosque underwent extension works on its north side during the reign of the Umayyad Governor Bishr Ibn Safwan (103/722–109/728) before being renovated by Yazid Ibn Hatim in 155/772. But the mosque, in the form and dimensions it takes today, is the work of the Aghlabid Prince Ziyadat Allah I who, in 221/836, demolished the entire building and built it up again in its entirety. In 247/862, Abu Ibrahim Ahmad added a narthex gallery built against the prayer room and surmounted by a dome. The enclosure of the Great Mosque of Kairouan is rectangular, measuring 125 m. in length and nearly 75 m. in width. From outside, the mosque looks like a fortress, prickling with towers and bastions and pierced by eight gates. In fact, this is due to the porches and buttresses that were added later on, essentially between the 7th/13th and 12th/18th century, in view of embellishing the mosque or of sustaining its Aghlabid walls which were definitely showing signs of decrepitude. This explains why a gate through the western facade (Bab al-Ma’ or Gate of the Water) as well as one belonging the eastern facade (Bab Lalla Rayhana) date from the reign of the Hafsid Caliph al-Mustansir, from 692/1293. The porch of the latter, surmounted by a superb fluted dome with stucco ornamentations, was erected by the *imam* of the Great Mosque in 716/1316. The other gates date either from the Muradite or the Husaynite periods.  
The central courtyard is surrounded by galleries displaying a rhythmic symphony of semi-circular horseshoe arches supported on columns and capitals taken from ancient sites. Thus, paradoxically, this mosque is the largest museum of Roman and Byzantine capitals ever to be formed under the roof of a single Muslim monument. The galleries that no doubt date from the time of Ziyadat Allah were certainly restored during the Hafsid era and then again in the Muradite era, as is attested to by a stone panel sculpted with floral motifs which can be seen in the south-west corner. An *impluvium*, whose labyrinth-like design consists of horseshoe arches, furnishes the centre of the courtyard. It no doubt dates from the era of Mohamed Bey (11th–12th/end of the 17th century). In the middle of the *qibla* gallery stands a dome on squinches called the dome of the *bahu*, which was completely renovated at the beginning of the 13th/19th century. In front, at the centre of the north side, rises the minaret built by Zidayat Allah. With a square-base foundation, it is composed of three levels reaching a height of 32 m. Its robust yet sober allure is a reminder of Roman lighthouses and of Syrian bell towers; it would become a model for future Ifriqiyan mosques up until the arrival of the Ottomans. The prayer room, formed in a hypostyle design in the Umayyad tradition, is composed of 17 naves and 8 bays, following the example of the Mosque of the Prophet in Medina. The crossing between the axial nave and the bay of the *qibla* forms a square on which a dome on squinches was erected, made of sculpted stone, whose forms and motifs (shells and polyfoiled rosettes) are of Umayyad inspiration. Most of the gates in the prayer hall, and essentially the central gate adorned with Maghrebi floral motifs, were re-built in 1244/1829. The prayer hall roof is made of wood. It was the object of several repairs throughout the ages. The oldest part dates from the 3rd/9th century; it has a pretty decor of flowers and foliage. The work undertaken by the Zirids during the 4th–5th/first half of the 9th century is marked by *kufic* inscriptions, the shafts of whose letters end in small, two-foiled flowers. The ceilings were restored under the Hafsids towards the end of the 7th/13th century. The last repairs date from the time of Murad I, in 1027/1618. The *mihrab* dates from the time of Abu Ibrahim Ahmad (247/862). It is adorned with a half-dome made of painted wood, and furnished with 28 fretted *champlevé* marble panels decorated with a variety of floral and geometric motifs, amongst which one can distinguish the vine leaf, in all its varied, stylised forms, as well as a shell design, inscribed within an arched bandwidth imitating the form of a *mihrab*. The decor, of Byzantine influence conveyed through Umayyad art from Syria, is as such imbued with Islamic creed. The frame of the *mihrab* niche is decorated with a unique collection of 139 tiles that have a metallic sheen, dating from the middle of the 3rd/9th century. Doubtless Iraqi in origin, this niche possesses a stylised floral ornamentation that can be viewed as a precursor to modern abstract art. The *minbar*, a jewel of Ifriqiyan art, dates from the middle of the 3rd/9th century, and is the oldest Muslim preaching pulpit to have survived. It consists of more than 300 Indian Teak wood panels. Its elaborate ornamentation, in which Byzantine and Mesopotamian influences are combined, denotes the maturity of Kairouanese art. The *maqsura*, situated to the right of the *minbar*, was built by the Zirid al-Mu‘izz in the 4th–5th/beginning of the 11th century. It enabled princes and governors to pray separately from the rest of the worshippers. Made of cedarwood, it is distinguished by its beautiful epigraphic frieze, written in flowery *kufic* script. The panels above this frieze were completely restored in the Ottoman era (1075/1665).

es.name: Mezquita Mayor
description:
La Mezquita Mayor de Kairuán es una de las más antiguas y está considerada como el más prestigioso santuario del Occidente islámico. Ha servido como modelo para la casi totalidad de las mezquitas de Ifriqiya y del Magreb, hasta la llegada de los otomanos. Por la diversidad de sus formas y la riqueza de su repertorio ornamental, encarna lo esencial de los elementos de la escuela arquitectónica de Kairuán. El primer oratorio fue edificado en el año 50/670 por Uqba ibn Nafi. Como que fue construido con material algo quebradizo, tuvo que ser posteriormente renovado por completo por Hassan Ibn Nu‘man en el año 84/703. La mezquita sufrió también ampliaciones en su parte norte, en época del gobernador omeya Bichr ibn Safwan (103/722-109/728), antes de ser renovada por Yazid ibn Hatim en el 155/772. Sin embargo, en lo que se refiere a su morfología y dimensiones actuales, esta mezquita debe considerarse como una obra del príncipe aglabí Ziyadat Allah I, quien en el año 221/836 demolió todo el edificio y luego lo reconstruyó completamente. En el año 247/862, Abu Ibrahim Ahmad añadió una galería apoyada a la sala de oración y una cúpula. La superficie de la gran mezquita dibuja un rectángulo de 125 m de largo por unos 75 de ancho. Vista desde el exterior, aparece como una fortaleza con torres y bastiones, abierta por ocho puertas. De hecho, se trata de porches y contrafuertes que fueron añadidos, esencialmente en el siglo VII/XIII y hasta el XII/XVIII, quizá con intención de embellecer la mezquita, aunque también pudiera ser para sostener los muros aglabíes, que parecían romperse. Fue así como se construyeron la Puerta del Agua (*bab el-ma*) sobre la fachada occidental y la Puerta Lalla Rayhana en la fachada oriental; ambas datan del reinado del califa hafsí el-Mustansir en 692/1293. El porche de esta última, coronada por una soberbia cúpula acanalada y decorada en estuco, fue erigido por el imam de la gran mezquita en 716/1316. Las otras puertas datan de las épocas muradí y husseiní.  
El patio central está rodeado por galerías que ofrecen una sinfonía ritmada de arcos de medio punto sobre capiteles y columnas tomados de los enclaves de la antigüedad. Así, paradójicamente, esta mezquita constituye el más grande de los museos de capiteles romanos y bizantinos jamás reunidos en un monumento islámico tunecino. Las galerías, que datan sin duda de la época de Ziyadat Allah, seguramente fueron restauradas en la época hafsí y luego muradí, como queda atestiguado en un panel de piedra esculpida con motivos florales que se encuentra en el ángulo sudoeste. Un impluvio, cuya decoración laberíntica está formada por arcos de medio punto, amuebla el centro del patio. Data sin duda de la época de Mohamed Bey, es decir, siglos XIXII/f. XVII. En medio de la galería de la *qibla* se sitúa una cúpula sobre trompas, llamada cúpula de *bahu*, completamente restaurada a principios del siglo XIII/XIX.  
Enfrente, en medio del muro norte, se eleva el alminar edificado por Ziyadat Allah. Es de base cuadrada y está formado por tres pisos superpuestos que superan los 32 m2. Su aire robusto y sobrio no deja de recordar los faros romanos y los campanarios sirios; su modelo servirá como ejemplo para otras mezquitas ifriqíes hasta la llegada de los otomanos.  
De forma hipóstila y tradición omeya, la sala de oración está compuesta de 17 naves dispuestas en 8 tramos, siguiendo el ejemplo de la mezquita del profeta en Medina. La zona en la que se encuentran la nave axial y el tramo de la *qibla* forma un cuadrado sobre el cual aparece una cúpula sobre trompas, en piedras esculpidas, cuyas formas y motivos en conchas-arcos y polilobulados rosetones se inspiran en el repertorio omeya. La mayoría de las puertas de la sala de oración, sobre todo la puerta central, están adornadas con motivos florales magrebíes y fueron restauradas en 1244/1829. La cubierta de la sala de oración ha sido edificada en madera y fue objeto de numerosas reconstrucciones a través de los tiempos. La parte más antigua data del siglo III/IX y presenta una alegre decoración con hojas y ramos en floreros.  
La obra de los ziríes, en los siglos IV-V/p.m. XI, se caracteriza por las inscripciones cúficas, cuya caligrafía queda terminada en trazos que forman flores bilobuladas. Los techos fueron restaurados en época hafsí, a finales del siglo VII/XIII. Las últimas reconstrucciones datan del reinado de Murad I, en 1027/1618.  
El mihrab data de la época de Abu Ibrahim Ahmad (247/862). Está coronado por semicúpulas de madera pintada, y decorado con 28 paneles de mármol calado o tallados en hueco que muestran una decoración compuesta por una amplia variedad de motivos florales y geométricos, entre los cuales se distingue la hoja de parra estilizada con diferentes formas, y una decoración que va formando conchas, inscrita en una banda arqueada que dibuja la forma de un *mihrab*. La decoración está marcada por las influencias bizantinas traídas al Magreb a través del arte omeya de Siria, donde se impregnó también del credo musulmán. El marco del nicho del *mihrab* está adornado con una colección única de 139 azulejos con reflejos metálicos, de mediados del siglo III/IX. Este nicho, seguramente de origen iraquí, está adornado con motivos florales estilizados que anuncian ya el arte abstracto moderno. El púlpito o *minbar* es una joya del arte de Ifriqiya y data de mediados del siglo III/IX; es el *minbar* musulmán más antiguo que ha llegado hasta nosotros. Está hecho a base de 300 paneles de madera de teca india. Esta riqueza en la ornamentación, en la que se combinan influencias bizantinas y mesopotámicas, denota la madurez del arte de Kairuán.  
La *maqsura*, situada a la derecha del *minbar*, fue construida por el zirí el-Mu‘izz entre los siglos IV-V/p. XI. Permitía a los príncipes y gobernadores hacer la oración de forma separada del resto de los fieles. Hecha en madera de cedro, se caracteriza por su bello friso epigráfico escrito en cúfico florido. Los paneles que se encuentran debajo de este friso fueron restaurados completamente en época otomana (1075/1665).

fr.name: La Grande Mosquée
description: La Grande Mosquée de Kairouan est considérée comme le plus ancien et le plus prestigieux sanctuaire dans l’Occident musulman. Son modèle architectural a servi d’exemple pour la majorité des mosquées ifriqiyennes jusqu’à l’arrivée des Ottomans. Par la diversité de ses formes et la richesse de son répertoire ornemental, elle incarne l’essentiel des éléments de l’école kairouanaise d’architecture. Le premier oratoire fut édifié en 50/670, par Oqba Ibn Nafi. Construit en matière friable, il fut complètement rénové par Hassan Ibn Nu‘man en 84/703. La mosquée subit des agrandissements du côté nord à l’époque du gouverneur omeyyade Bichr Ibn Safwan (103/722-109/728) avant d’être renouvelée par Yazid Ibn Hatim en 155/772. Mais la mosquée, dans ses morphologie et dimension actuelles, est l’oeuvre du prince aghlabide Ziyadat Allah I qui, en 221/836, démolit tout l’édifice et le reconstruisit complètement. En 247/862, Abou Ibrahim Ahmad ajouta une galerie narthex adossée à la salle de prière et surmontée d’une coupole. L’enceinte de la Grande Mosquée de Kairouan dessine un rectangle de 125 m de longueur et presque 75 m de largeur. Extérieurement, elle apparaît comme une forteresse hérissée de tours et bastions et percée de huit portes. En fait, il s’agit de porches et de contreforts qui furent ajoutés, essentiellement du VIIe/XIIIe jusqu’au XIIe/XVIIIe siècle, en vue d’embellir la mosquée ou de soutenir ses murs aghlabides qui présentaient certainement des signes de décrépitude. C’est ainsi qu’une porte de la façade occidentale (Bab el-Ma’ ou Porte de l’Eau) et une de la façade orientale (Bab Lalla Rayhana) datent du règne du calife hafside el-Moustansir, en 692/1293. Le porche de cette dernière, surmonté d’une superbe coupole à cannelures et orné de décors en stucs fut érigé par l’Imam de la Grande Mosquée, en 716/1316. Les autres portes datent de l’époque mouradite et husseinite. La cour centrale est entourée de galeries qui offrent une symphonie rythmée d’arcs en plein cintre outrepassés qui reposent sur des chapiteaux et colonnes provenant de sites anciens. Ainsi, paradoxalement, cette mosquée constitue le plus grand musée de chapiteaux romains et byzantins jamais réunis dans un monument musulman. Les galeries qui datent sans doute de l’époque de Ziyadat Allah furent certainement restaurées à l’époque hafside puis mouradite, comme l’atteste un panneau de pierre sculpté de motifs floraux se trouvant à l’angle sud-ouest. Un impluvium, dont le décor labyrinthique est formé d’arcs outrepassés, meuble le centre de la cour. Il date sans doute de l’époque de Mohamed Bey (XIe-XIIe/f. XVIIe siècle). Au milieu de la galerie de la *qibla* se dresse une coupole sur trompes dite coupole du *bahou*, complètement renouvelée au début du XIIIe/XIXe siècle. En face et au milieu du côté nord, s’élève le minaret qui fut édifié par Ziyadat Allah. De base carrée, il est formé de trois étages superposés atteignant 32 m de hauteur. Son allure robuste et sobre n’est pas sans nous rappeler les phares romains et les clochers syriens; son modèle servira d’exemple pour les autres mosquées ifriqiyennes jusqu’à l’arrivée des Ottomans. La salle de prière, de forme hypostyle et de tradition omeyyade, est composée, à l’exemple de la mosquée du Prophète à Médine, de 17 nefs et de 8 travées. La rencontre entre la nef axiale et la travée de la *qibla* détermine un carré sur lequel fut érigée une coupole sur trompes, en pierres sculptées dont les formes et motifs (coquilles, rosaces polylobées) s’inspirent du répertoire omeyyade. La plupart des portes de la salle de prière et essentiellement la porte centrale, ornée de motifs floraux maghrébins, furent renouvelées en 1244/1829. La couverture de la salle de prière est faite en bois. Elle fut l’objet de plusieurs réfections à travers les âges. La partie la plus ancienne date du IIIe/IXe siècle; elle présente un joli décor de rinceaux et fleurons. L’oeuvre des Zirides, au cours du IVe-Ve/p.m. XIe siècle, se caractérise par des inscriptions coufiques dont les hampes des lettres se terminent par des fleurons bilobés. Les plafonds furent restaurés sous les Hafsides, à la fin du VIIe/XIIIe siècle. Les dernières réfections datent de l’époque de Mourad I, en 1027/1618. Le *mihrab* date de l’époque de Abou Ibrahim Ahmad (247/862). Il est coiffé de demi-coupoles en bois peint et meublé par vingt-huit panneaux de marbre ajouré ou champlevé qui offrent un décor composé d’une variété de motifs floraux et géométriques parmi lesquels se distinguent la feuille de vigne stylisée sous ses différentes formes et un décor en coquille, inscrit dans un bandeau arqué élaborant la forme d’un *mihrab*. Le décor, marqué par des influences byzantines, véhiculé par l’art omeyyade de Syrie, s’imprègne ainsi du credo musulman. L’encadrement de la niche du *mihrab* est orné par une collection unique de 139 carreaux de faïence à reflets métalliques, datables du milieu du IIIe/IXe siècle. Sans doute d’origine irakienne, cette niche est ornée de motifs floraux stylisés qui annoncent déjà l’art abstrait moder-ne. Le *minbar*, joyau de l’art ifriqiyen, date du milieu du IIIe/IXe siècle et constitue la plus ancienne chaire à prêcher musulmane qui nous soit parvenue. Elle est faite de plus de 300 panneaux en bois de teck indien. La richesse de l’ornementation, dans laquelle se combinent les influences byzantines et mésopotamiennes, dénote de la maturité de l’art kairouanais. La *maqsoura*, située à droite du *minbar*, fut édifiée par le ziride el-Mu‘izz, au IVe-Ve/d. XIe siècle. Elle permet aux princes et gouverneurs d’effectuer la prière à l’écart des autres fidèles. Faite en bois de cèdre, elle se distingue par sa belle frise épigraphique, écrite en coufique fleuri. Les panneaux se trouvant au-dessous de cette frise furent complètement restaurés à l’époque ottomane (1075/1665).

cs.name: Dominikánský kostel sv. Michala, Brno
description: Douvěžové pručelí členěné pilastry a lizénami završuje trojúhelný štít s patronem kostela ve vrcholu. Sochy A. Rigy byly do nik prolamujících jinak plochou fasádu osazeny až r. 1728. Ke kostelu, na nějž navazují budovy kláštera, byla přistavěna kaple Božího hrobu v gotických formách (1701). Jednolodní sálový prostor s bočními kaplemi zaplňují dva bloky bohatě řezaných lavic zdobených akantovými rozvilinami.

Kostel byl sněmovním chrámem moravských stavů, zasedajících v přilehlém klášteře. Z důvodu urbanistického začlenění novostavby na Rybném trhu byla obrácena orientace kostela, do nějž se nyní vstupuje od východu. Statické problémy si již po dokončení stavby zasazené do svahu vyžádaly úpravy jejichž součástí bylo i vytvoření terasy, osazené sochami. Na vybavení oltářů kostela se podíleli přední brněnští umělci. Pozoruhodná je sochařsky ztvárněná kazatelna s padlými anděly. K některým částem výzdoby se dochovaly přípravné skicy.
artist: Jan Křtitel Erna (1625? Brno – 1698 Brno), Domenico Martinelli (1650 Lucca – 1718 Lucca), Anton Riga (kolem 1660 Královec – 1728 Brno), Josef Winterhalder st. (1702 Vöhrenbach – 1769 Vídeň), Damascenus Schwarz, Dominik Kirchner, Johann Franz Greipel (1720–1798), Josef Tadeáš Rotter (1701 Opava – 1763 Brno), Johann Lukas Kracker (1717 Vídeň – 1779 Eger), Josef Stern (1716 Štýrský Hradec – 1775 Brno), František Vavřinec Korompay (1723 Rohatec u Strážnice – 1779 Brno), Josef Winterhalder ml. (1743 Vöhrenbach – 1807 Znojmo), Karl Aigen, Jan Adam Nesmann (1710 Mohuč – 1773 Brno), Ondřej Schweigl (1735 Brno – 1812 Brno), Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc)
history: Kostel byl sněmovním chrámem moravských stavů, zasedajících v přilehlém klášteře. Z odkazu zemského sudího Lva z Kounic, jenž zde založil hrobku Kouniců, byl původně středověký kostel zcela přestavěn. Urbanistické začlenění novostavby si vyžádalo obrácení orientace kostela, do nějž se nyní vstupuje od východu. Statické problémy si již po dokončení stavby J. K. Ernou vyžádaly úpravy. Staré pohledy na náměstí, kde se nacházel také markraběcí dům a mincovna, představují monumentální působení chrámu v tehdejší zástavbě.

en.name: Dominican Church of St. Michael, Brno
description: The two-spire frontage which is segmented with pilasters and lesenes culminates in a triangular gable on top of which is the patron saint of the church. In 1728, in order to break up the flat façade, statues by A. Riga were set in niches. The mock-Gothic Chapel of the Holy Grave was added in 1701. The single-nave church adjoining the monastery buildings is flanked by side chapels furnished by blocks of richly carved pews decorated with acanthus leafs.

The church was frequented by Moravian estate-holders who held their sessions in the adjacent monastery. City development incorporated the new church into what was the fish market, so that its disposition was reversed and the building was entered from the east. Setting the church into a mild slope quickly caused problems; repairs included the construction of a terrace lined with statues. The church altars were decorated by leading Brno artists. The pulpit with sculpted fallen angels is particularly noteworthy. Sketches for some parts of the decoration have been preserved.
artist: Jan Křtitel Erna (1625? Brno – 1698 Brno), Anton Riga (cca 1660 Kaliningrad – 1728 Brno), Josef Winterhalder Sr. (1702 Vöhrenbach – 1769 Vienna), Damascenus Schwarz, Dominik Kirchner, Johan Franz Greipel (1720–1798), Josef Tadeáš Rotter (1701 Opava – 1763 Brno), Johann Lukas Kracker (1717 Vienna –1779 Eger), Josef Stern (1716 Graz – 1775 Brno), František Vavřinec Korompay (1723 Rohatec u Strážnice – 1779 Brno), Josef Winterhalder Jr. (1743 Vöhrenbach – 1807 Znojmo), Karl Aigen, Jan Adam Nesmann (1710 Mainz – 1773 Brno), Ondřej Schweigl (1735–1812, Brno), Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc)
history: The church was frequented by Moravian estate holders who held their sessions in the adjacent monastery. The complete refurbishment of the original medieval church was financed by the legacy of the provincial judge, Lev of Kounice, who had established the Kounic family tomb there. City development incorporated the new church into what was the fish market, so its disposition was reversed and the building was entered from the east. Setting the church into a mild slope proved a problem shortly after its completion by J. K. Erna. Old views of the square, which also featured the margrave’s house and a mint, show the monumental effect of the church amidst the surrounding buildings.
keywords: Allegory, Jesuits, re-Catholicization

en.name: Les fortifications du port
description:
In 935 / 1529, Khair-Eddine Barbarossa destroyed the fortress of Peñon, held by the Spanish on one of the port’s islets in order to control trade to and from the port. Thus he ended Spanish rule of al-Djazair (Algiers). The construction of a jetty linking the islets to the city was the starting point for changes to the port, and at the same time his first major military action in Algiers.  
  
Despite resistance by the Spanish garrison and its leader Martin de Vargas, Khair-Eddine Barbarossa finally won after three weeks of fighting, and he used materials from the destroyed fortress to build a 300-metre long pier, creating a dock with a levee for protection against the waves. After filling in the gaps between islands, he created a second north-south jetty, giving the port its general form, which lasted through the Ottoman era: two perpendicular jetties that nearly enclosed the harbour. A chain closed the port every night. After this phase, which lasted until 962 / 1555, the military protection of the waterfront would become the major concern of the governors of al-Djazair.  
  
From the second half of the 10th / 16th century, the port would be the scene of uninterrupted construction, with various phases of fortification in response to threats of enemy attacks. In 980 / 1573, the beylerbey Arab Ahmed, learning of preparations for war by Don Juan of Austria, and thinking they would be directed against Algiers, ordered construction of the first two towers of the port: Bordj al-Fanar (Tower of the Lighthouse or Lantern), on the site of the former Peñon, and Bordj Ras al-Moul (Tower at Pier’s End). The former, upon which the lantern was erected, has a circular shape 60 metres in diameter on four floors of embrasures for artillery. It is the most imposing structure in this part of the port. It would be renovated and consolidated in 1028 / 1619.  
  
Between 1063 / 1665 and 1068 / 1658, various pashas continued the work by adding Bordj Sardin (Fort of Sardines, so-called because of its commemorative inscription decorated with fish), Bordj al-Djadid (New Fort), completed in 1773 / 1186, and Bordj al-Gouman (Fort of Cables), rebuilt in 1230 / 1815. Finally, Bordj Ma Bayn (Fort in the Middle) filled the space between two fortifications in the centre of the pier in 1231 / 1816.  
  
These forts connect to each other through vaulted passages protected from external attacks. They form a continuous line of defence in front of the city. Thanks to these six fortifications, Algiers earned its name of “Mahroussa” – “well-guarded”.  
  
Just behind this first line of defence ran the second defence along the city’s coastline. It corresponded to the seaside part of the rampart that encircled the city on its other sides. Nine out of 15 batteries remain. It is the most heavily armed portion of the wall, intended to face marine attacks. The most important batteries are concentrated near the pier. Toppanet al-Goumrag (Bastion of Customs) is located near the store where taxes on imported goods were recorded and collected. Also on the waterfront are Bordj Bab al-Bahr (Bastion of the Sea Gate), with two levels of embrasures and 15 cannons, and Bordj Djamaa al-Kabir (Bastion of the Great Mosque), with three arrowslits, on the path that surrounds the mosque of the same name.

fr.name: Les fortifications du port
description:
En 935/1529, Khair-Eddine Barberousse détruisait la forteresse du Peñon que les Espagnols détenaient sur un des îlots du port, entravant tout commerce, et mettait ainsi un terme à l’emprise espagnole sur la ville. Point de départ de tous les futurs aménagements du port, la construction d’une jetée reliant les îlots à la ville constitue en même temps sa première action militaire d’envergure à al-Djazaïr.  
  
Malgré la résistance de la garnison espagnole et de son chef Martin de Vargas, Khair-Eddine finit par l’emporter après trois semaines de combat et utilise les matériaux de construction de la forteresse détruite pour aménager un môle de 300 mètres de long créant une darse avec mur de protection contre les vagues. Après avoir comblé les espaces entre les îles, il crée un second terre-plein orienté nord-sud, conférant au port la forme générale, qu’il gardera pendant toute l’époque ottomane, de deux jetées perpendiculaires avec un retour légèrement refermé. Une chaîne ferme le port tous les soirs. Après la phase de comblement qui dure jusqu’en 962/1555, la protection militaire du front de mer ainsi créé va être le souci majeur des gouverneurs d’al-Djazaïr.  
  
Dès la seconde moitié du Xe/XVIe siècle, le port sera le théâtre de travaux ininterrompus, les différentes phases de fortification répondant aux menaces des attaques ennemies. Ainsi, en 980/1573, le beylerbey Arab Ahmed, informé de préparatifs de guerre de Don Juan d’Autriche et les pensant dirigés contre Alger, fait construire les deux premières tours du port : Bordj al-Fanar (tour du Phare ou de la Lanterne), sur l’emplacement de l’ancien Peñon, et Bordj Ras al-Moul (tour du Bout du môle). Le premier ouvrage, sur lequel est érigé le phare, épouse une forme circulaire de 60 mètres de diamètre sur quatre étages d’embrasures pour l’artillerie. C’est l’oeuvre la plus importante dans cette partie du port. Elle sera remaniée et consolidée en 1028/1619.  
  
Entre 1063/1665 et 1068/1658, les différents pachas continuent le travail de leurs prédécesseurs en ajoutant Bordj Sardin (fort des Sardines, ainsi nommé en raison de son inscription commémorative décorée de poissons), Bordj al-Djadid (fort Neuf), terminé en 1773/1186, et Bordj al-Gouman (fort des Câbles), reconstruit en 1230/1815. Enfin, Bordj Ma Bayn (fort du Milieu) vient combler l’espace entre deux *bordj*s au centre du môle, en 1231/1816.  
  
Ces forts communiquent entre eux par des passages voûtés protégés des attaques extérieures. Ils présentent une ligne de défense continue en avant de la ville. Grâce à ces six bordjs, Alger méritait son nom de “*Mahroussa*”, la “bien gardée”.  
Juste en arrière de cette première ligne défensive se déploie la deuxième ligne sur le littoral bordant la ville. Elle correspond à la partie, sur mer, du rempart encerclant la ville sur ses autres côtés. On y trouve neuf batteries sur les quinze qui protègent la cité. C’est la façade la mieux armée de la muraille car destinée à faire face aux attaques venant de la mer. Les batteries les plus importantes sont concentrées près du môle. Toppanet al-Goumrag (bastion de la Douane) est situé près du magasin où l’on enregistrait et encaissait les impôts sur les marchandises importées. Citons aussi, toujours sur le front de mer, Bordj Bab al-Bahr (bastion de la porte de la Mer), avec deux niveaux d’embrasures et quinze canons, et Bordj Djamaa al-Kabir (bastion de la Grande Mosquée), avec trois meurtrières, sur le chemin de ronde de la mosquée du même nom.

en.name: Naval Dockyard
description: The naval dockyard, which was built several years after the construction of the port, stands as an architectural complex which is in partial ruin. It includes a series of storage spaces 7 m. wide and 18 m. deep, covered by barrel vaults on beams. These storage spaces are preceded by a gallery which was used as a shed to shelter the boats which were taken out of the water. Other than the store rooms and the gallery, this naval dockyard included two penal prisons, housing both the warder and Christian slaves, who were employed in the naval constructions; it very probably included a chapel for them to practise their faith.

es.name: Arsenal
description: El arsenal fue construido algunos años después del arreglo general del puerto. Actualmente se trata de un complejo arquitectónico parcialmente en ruinas. Cuenta con una larga serie de grandes almacenes de 7 m de ancho por 18 m de largo, cubiertos con bóvedas de cañón sobre una gran viga maestra. Aparecen precedidos por una galería, que servía de cobertizo destinado a proteger durante un tiempo los navíos que llegaban a puerto. Este arsenal tenía, además del almacén y las galerías, dos lugares especiales para el alojamiento de los esclavos cristianos dedicados a la construcción naval y para los remeros. Probablemente contenía también una capilla para el culto.

fr.name: L’arsenal
description: L’arsenal, qui a été construit quelques années après l’aménagement du port, est un complexe architectural partiellement en ruine. Il compte une série de grands magasins de 7 m de large sur 18 m de profondeur, couverts de voûtes en berceau sur doubleaux. Ces magasins sont précédés d’une galerie qui servait de remise destinée à mettre à couvert les navires qu’on tirait à sec. Cet arsenal comptait, outre le magasin et les galeries, deux bagnes pour le logement des esclaves chrétiens affectés à la construction navale et la chiourme; il comprenait fort probablement une chapelle pour l’exercice de leur culte.

ar.name: مشكاة.
description:
مشكاة مستطيلة الشكل، عمقها مستدير على شكل صدفة مزيّنة بعروق تنتهي بتجاويف. زُيِّنت فتحة الواجهة، المنحوتة بقليل من البروز، بإكليليّات زهريّة ومعيّنات ودوائر، بينما غُطيت الركنيّات برصائع ذات وُريدات تحيط بها من الجهتين أوراق نباتية منمنمة.  
يحيط بالكوّة إطار مزدوج: الإطار الأوّل مؤلّف من شريط ذو تشبيكات على شكل معيّنات، والثاني من شريط ضيّق مخرّم.  
تُذكّر زخرفة هذه اللوحة بالزخارف التي كان الرومان وبيزنطيّو شمال إفريقيا ينحتونها على مذاخر مصنوعة من الطين وعلى عناصر معمارية ومذابح … إلخ.، ممّا يشهد على استمراريّة السّجلّ التزييني.  
كان النحت يُنفّذ بواسطة نصلٍ حديدي يستعمل على التمشنت (الجبس المحلّي) وهو لازال رخواً. واستناداً إلى رأي هنري سالادان، فإنّ هذا الجبس المحلي المصنوع من الحجر الكلسيّ الخاص بالمنطقة كان "يُطبّق على جدران من التراب المدكوك أو من الحجر الدبش".  
كانت المشكاة مبنية في زاوية غرفة على ارتفاعٍ معيّن من الأرض. وقد خضع قسمها العلوي للترميم.

مشكاة ذات عمق مستدير وقبة نصفية تحمل على الواجهة زخرفة جصية محلية (نقش حديدة)، مكونة من زخارف هندسية بسيطة أو زهرية على شكل وريدات، مشكلة من التمنشيت. أعدت هذه المشكاة في زاوية إحدى الغرف الكبيرة؛ وكانت تستعمل كدولاب، وتساهم في حمل السقف.
dynasty: الفترة الرستمية، 161 - 296 هجري / 778 - 909 ميلادي؛ رستميّو سدراتة، 296 - 467 هجري / 909 - 1074 ميلادي

en.name: Niche.
description:
Rectangular-shaped niche with a rounded back in the form of a shell, ornamented with fillets that end in roll mouldings. The façade of the bay, which is sculpted in bas-relief, is decorated with festoons, lozenges and circles, whereas the cornerstones are adorned with rosettes framed on either side with stylised leaves.  
The bay fits within a double frame: the first formed by a lozenge trellis, the second by a narrow fret band.  
The decoration of this panel evokes that sculpted by the Romans and the Byzantines from North Africa on shrines that were made of earth, as well as on architectural pieces, altars, etc., all of which attests to the continuity of the ornamental repertory.  
The sculpture was executed with a metal blade, worked on the *timchent* while it was still soft. According to H. Saladin (see Bibliography) this local type of plaster made from the region's limestone was 'applied to walls made of cobblestones or rubble'.  
The niche was built in the corner of a room at a certain height above ground-level. The upper part has undergone restoration work.

Niche with a rounded back and a half-dome whose façade bears *naqsh-hadida* (sculpted plaster) decoration with simple geometric or floral rosette motifs in *timchent* plaster. Placed in the corner of a large room, it would have been used as a cupboard and also to help support the ceiling.
holder: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Arts
keywords: Niche; shell; plaster; timchent; sculpture; Palatial architecture; geometric decoration; Rustamid; Sedrata; rectangular case; monument; construction; geometric adornment; rosette; local plaster
partner: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Art

es.name: Hornacina.
description:
Hornacina de frontal rectangular y fondo en forma de concha con nervios rematados por celdillas. El arco, esculpido en bajorrelieve, está decorado con festones, rombos y círculos, mientras que las enjutas están rellenas de rosetones rodeados de hojas estilizadas.  
El vano está inscrito en un doble marco: el primero, formado por una banda con un entramado romboidal, y el segundo, por una estrecha cinta calada.  
La decoración de esta hornacina recuerda la que los romanos y bizantinos del norte de África esculpían sobre relicarios de barro, elementos arquitectónicos, altares, etc., lo que atestigua la continuidad del repertorio ornamental.  
La talla se hacía con una hoja de hierro sobre el *timshent* todavía blando. Según H. Saladin, este yeso local, obtenido a partir de la piedra caliza propia de la región, “se aplicaba sobre muros en adobe o en morrillo”.  
La hornacina estaba colocada en un ángulo, a cierta altura del suelo. La parte superior ha sido restaurada.

Hornacina de fondo redondeado y coronado con una semicúpula. El frontal, decorado con la técnica llamada n*aqsh hadida*, muestra sencillos motivos geométricos o florales en forma de rosetones labrados en *timshent* (yeso local). Estaba situado en el ángulo de una sala grande, a modo de armario.
holder: Museo Nacional de Antigüedades y Arte Islámico
keywords: nicho; concha; yeso; timshent; escultura; arquitectura palatina; decoración geométrica; rustamíes; Sedrata
partner: Museo Nacional de Antigüedades y de Arte Islámico

fr.name: Niche.
description:
Niche de plan rectangulaire à fond arrondi sous forme de coquille ornée de nervures terminées par des alvéoles. La baie de façade, sculptée en faible relief, est ornée de festons, de losanges et de cercles, tandis que les écoinçons sont meublés de médaillons à rosaces cernés de part et d'autre par des feuilles stylisées.  
La baie s'inscrit dans un double encadrement : le premier formé d'une bande à treillis losangé, le second d'une étroite bande ajourée.  
Le décor de ce panneau évoque celui que les Romains et les Byzantins du nord de l'Afrique sculptaient sur des reliquaires en terre, des éléments architecturaux, des autels, etc., ce qui atteste la continuité du répertoire ornemental.  
La sculpture était exécutée à l'aide d'une lame en fer sur le *timchent* alors qu'il était encore mou. Selon H. Saladin, ce plâtre local élaboré à partir de la pierre calcaire propre à la région était “appliqué sur des murs en pisé ou en moellons”.  
La niche était aménagée dans un angle de pièce à une certaine hauteur au-dessus du sol. La partie supérieure a subi une restauration.

Niche à fond arrondi et demi-coupole portant sur la façade un décor en *noukch-hadida* à motif géométrique simple ou floral en rosaces, façonné dans du *timchent*. Aménagée dans l'angle d'une grande pièce, elle servait de placard, tout en contribuant à soutenir le toit.
holder: Musée national des antiquités et des arts islamiques
keywords: niche ; coquille ; plâtre ; timchent ; sculpture ; architecture palatine ; décor géométrique ; Rostémides ; Sédrata
partner: Le Musée national des antiquités et d’art musulman

en.name: Italian military conscription office in Tunis
short_description: Under terms of an 1896 agreement with France, Italy ran a military conscription office in Tunis. It was through this office that Italy drafted its migrants in Tunisia for the war on Turkey in 1911-12 and for the First World War. During WWI, many Italians living in Tunisia, because of their knowledge of the French language.  were assigned to the military units posted in France. Many of them died or were crippled for life. After the war, the Italian government opened a War Pensions Bureau in Tunis.

en.name: Islamic pottery from Ephesus
short_description: Excavated by John Turtle Wood, an architect and surveyor. He was employed by the Ottoman Railway Company from 1858. Between 1863–1874 he excavated on behalf of the British Museum at ancient Ephesus, where he discovered the Temple of Artemis.
keywords: archaeology

en.name: Lattice design carpet fragment
description:
A 17th century Safavid Kirman pile carpet fragment. Uncommonly long and narrow, it is decorated with a single-plane lattice design on a dark blue background. The carpet's lattice structure is made up of long red serrated leaves linked together by round yellow-coloured flowers. The lattice’s compartments each holds a one of a variety of flowering plants, including irises, carnations, narcissi, lotuses and roses; all of which are organised in a directional fashion, giving the carpet design a top and a bottom.  
  
Even though this carpet is a fragment, upon close technical examination of its foundation’s structure, its width was found to be complete, indicating that the carpet was purposefully woven with no left and right borders. However, its top and bottom ends are now missing. The shape of this carpet fragment, especially its narrowness, suggests that it may have been made to cover a specific floor space that required it not to have any conventional borders.
keywords: leaf lattice; floral motifs; fragment; iris; carnation; narcissus; lotus; Kerman
materials: Cotton warp; wool and cotton weft; wool pile

en.name: *St. George Church*
short_description: Built by Monsignor Joseph Debs, the neo-classical cathedral was inspired by the largest Catholic Marian church in Rome, the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore, and bears great resemblance to it. The construction of this church, dedicated to patron saint St George, was finished in 1894. Heavily hit and looted (including an important Delacroix painting of St Georges) during the Lebanese civil war it was finally restored and re-inaugurated in April 2000.
